That said we enjoyed our time Downtown and the location of the hotel is good especially for one/two night cruise passengers.

We found the hotel faultless, really clean, excellent service and really good value for money! Loved Angelina who served us every night in the lounge bar! Our only gripe was the area... We live in the NE of England so are used to a bit of rough and tumble but upon leaving the hotel each time we felt really uneasy!!! Too many hobos and drug addicts!!! !

This hotel lived up to its name and expectations! VERY clean and tidy The staff was great, courteous, and friendly. Our room had a great view of the city. The restaurant on the main level was excellent, had a variety of food and drinks. We had a small group and received a decent price for the weekend. The central fire station is located a few blocks down from this hotel. The valet was efficient and always had our car available when we exited the elevator.

I spent 2 nights here for a business trip. This is an older hotel but seems to have been renovated fairly recently. One annoyance, the first suite assigned to me was already occupied! Second room was upgrade to huge corner junior suite with nice view thru floor-ceiling windows of Biscayne Bay and cruise ship harbor. Hotel was packed with south american tourists but my corner room was quiet. Location is a little awkward to enter due to road construction. 2 sets of elevators and 2nd floor lobby layout is confusing at first. High parking rates unless you get park & stay AAA rate (I did). Good restaurant. Good Chinese restaurant in Doubletree next door. Room was in good condition and seemed fairly recent renovation.

Fridge didnt work Staff was rude and all spanish speaking. Staff lied that the bus system of Miami was very difficult to use when in fact it was more inexpensive and a lot easier than getting around w/ a taxi. Room was small and boring. Pool sucked Cooling system was messed up (we could not control it) We stayed there 5 days and really got tired of it!

query: hotel room cleanliness and bathroom hygiene

reviews.text: we are local but made a "staycation" out of my birthday celebration for a night. the romance package is worth the upgrade because it includes champagne, valet parking, chocolates and breakfast, and they even cover the bed with rose petals if/when you leave the room after check-in. if i had to nit pick i would say that a couple of lights switches and one of the phones did not work (ironic for a restored electric building) but in all honesty none of those defects affected our stay, which is probably why no one bothered to report them before; having said that a hotel of this stature should probably have better quality control so i still deducted one star from my rating. other than that the bathroom is not very private so if you want to preserve the "romance" factor you'll need to make a trip to the lobby because the ballroom level restroom is kept locked.

The Joule was a great hotel to stay at in Dallas. When we first arrived there was tea and cookies in the lobby waiting for all of the guest, with a fantastic array of decorations in the lobby. When we spoke to one of the front desk clerks they said it used to be a bank and it was to be designed along the lines of natural elements such as wind and water. When we got to our room it was very modern and high tech with all of the light switches and lamp knobs. However, we didn't reserve a handicap room but got oen anyway with two beds. The shower was GREAT, the beds were GREAT but the view was looking at airconditioners which didn't bother us because we weren't looking out that much. Also the maids probably need to consider dusting in the bathroom lights becuase they were covered in dust! We ate breakfest downstairs at Charlie Palmer which was one of the best hotel breakfest experiences I have ever had. The service was amazing and the food was amazing.

Stayed there for one night so I did not get to use any of the hotel services nor dine there. However, the staff were all very nice and helpful. They also have complimentary car service via a Cadillac Escalade which takes you and picks you up anywhere within 5 miles of the hotel. Truly a wonderful, and from my experience unique service. Being it is very contemporary, be prepared for glass shower and toilet doors. Bed was very plush and comfortable.

I read the reviews before I went so I addressed some of the service issues beforehand. My boyfriend and I stayed there for his birthday and I wanted everything to be perfect. Jessica, the front desk manager, was great. Their new GM is aware of the service issues they have had and he is working to turn it around. We were treated very well. They had a bottle of champagne,yummy chocolates and a cheese platter in the room. We stayed in one of the lofts and initially had some temperature issues but they were addressed quickly. The room was fantastic. Well decorated, sleek and modern. They have the top of the line Beautyrest mattress which was really comfortable. Two of the three bathrooms had huge walk in showers and double showerheads. The owner is an art collector so the lobby was decorated with pieces from his own personal collection. There is a sustainable energy theme in the hotel and Jessica and Brandon gave us the background story. If you go ask the front desk about it. Charlie Palmers is connected to the hotel and it is excellent. The sommelier at Charlie Palmers, Brandon was awesome. He coordinated with NOKA Chocolates for a private wine and chocolate pairing on Saturday afternoon. The pool area was packed and we had a cabana reserved for us. The pool is small but they keep it very cool and refreshing. It had a mini-Vegas poolside vibe. Their nightclub, PM, manages the pool area. We had opportunity to go to PM that night as well. We got the red carpet treatment. They had initially reserved us a table but when we got there it had been given away. They apologized profusely and comped us all our drinks. I would say that this place is worth a chance despite the reviews. The staff seems very willing to hear feedback and make it better. We had a lovely, relaxing weekend.

This is a great hotel to visit. The staff for the most part are excellent and helpful. For the most part the staff doesnt have all the attitude that the W staff does. Some of the younger front desk staff tend to be a little snooty. but for the most part, the staff is excellent. The concierge is very helpful and knows his stuff. The manager of the attached restaurantis also really helpful and provides excellent service - even though the restaurant is independently managed. The rooms are awesome except for the lack of privacy in the toilets that others have mentioned. The view from the lower floors is kinda cruddy and the street noise might get loud on the weekend. Overall, can't wait to come back.

The Joule Dallas is a hoteliers dream. All of the details from the lobby theme and decor to the functional and modern bathrooms have been impeccably taken care of. The beds are luxurious and will envelop you in dream inducing comfort. The clean lines and technically savvy components of the guest rooms ensure that you remain at ease and connected while you travel. The staff is professional and accommodating of all needs. Great hotel that should not be missed!

My husband and I stayed at the Joule In late January. We stayed in a deluxe room. It was by no means big, but it was perfect for two. We both loved the shower. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We used the free car service several times and the drivers all had great recommendations for places to go and to eat. We wish the weather had been warmer so we could have tried out the pool. My only complaint about our room was that one side faced east and the bathroom window was not adequately covered so the morning sun lit up the whole room. Not great if you're trying to sleep in.

Stayed here for a leisure weekend. Downtown area around it is sort of dead... the structure itself is a period building, renovated into a boutique hotel. Lobby is very nice, if a bit "tries to hard" and dark. Restaurant very nice for breakfast. Rooms also nice, well-maintained, if again trying a bit too hard - one almost feels like this hotel is screaming "yes, I know its Dallas, but Dallas can be trendy too!". I wasn't crazy about the way the bathroom is a bit open to the room. Very nice and helpful staff. Would certainly recommend any one stay here.

Stayed at this property the day before Valentines with my wife. We were impressed with how intimate and different this hotel is. It is definitely worth checking out while in Dallas. The decor is artsy and modern, great location, in a historic building. The room was beautifully appointed with a round bed, bvlagari amenities, rainfall shower, and oversized flat screen. The room was surprisingly small and the bed was terrible, i liked the idea of a round bed as it is unique but it was very awkward and felt cheap..not a luxury collection standard. We used the house car, a Cadillac Escalade which took us around, nice touch but the car wasnt as clean as it should have been and the driver didnt seem like he wanted to take us. Other than that no complaints, beautiful pool on the 10th floor and up to date fitness center with bottles of water and fruit. The Joule really is a gem and I would return but probably would opt for a different room catogory

There are probably more remote controls in these rooms than in any other hotel you have stayed in. The first time I stayed here, I arrived late and figuring out all the controls was maddening. But I have stayed here three times since and like the hotel. The staff is great and the hotel has a great Charlie Trotter restaurant. (But what's with the big wooden wheel in the lobby?)

Not only is this a great hotel, but I was traveling on business and experienced an illness during my trip. Not only did the hotel help me find a local doctor, but the manager on duty checked on me and sent chicken soup to the room to help me feel better. I wish i did not have to cut my trip short, because the pool looked like a lot of fun.

I travel at least once a month for work, and I was fortunate enough to stay at this hotel last February and it's such a charming hotel. The staff are courteous and professional, without overdoing it. The design and decor is incredible. The have really nice turn down service, too. The hotel and guest rooms are cozy without feeling too small. I would never hesitate to return to this hotel. I hope to be back.

Working with this hotel has been a breeze. Jessica and Byron were able to help organize my large group of 21 guests with ease. Every detail was managed perfectly. I am very happy with my stay. Thank you so much! Also, the hotel offers complimentary shoe shining service. -- LB

I stayed here for one night for a short business trip with meetings in Dallas downtown. This was part of the Starwood Luxury Collection, but having been dissappointed many times before, I did not expect much. Turns out I was way wrong. This was probably one of the best Starwod properties I have stayed in the last year. The hotel is about 40 minutes from DFW airport in downtown Dallas. Check in staff was extremely courteous and actually escorted me to the elevators (instead of saying "turn left, then right..." as the front deks often does). The front deks area is not huge, but has a farily open seating and meeting place. The room was spacious enough, with a big glass wall on the outside, a 42" flat screen TV, and terrific lighting arrangements that allowed you to adjust the brightness in various parts of the room. The bed was very comfy. Everything was clean and well maintained. The bath and toilet were divided into two separate rooms, and the sink area was separate. This can be useful for couples staying in the room. There was a complimentary bottle of water, and toiletries were top notch. There was a nice collection of magazines in a rack next to the toilet bowl! Internet cost the usual $12 to $14 a day. Just one downside. The area around the hotel isn't exactly swanky. There are a lot of office buildings, but the place really seems to die down after 5 PM. There is a Neiman Marcus and a decent Mexican restaurant next door, but there's also a boarded up building.

This was, simply the best hotel experience we have ever had. My wife and I stayed at this hotel to celebrate our anniversary. Upon check in, they knew (and remembered!) our names, what we liked, everyone congratulated us on our anniversary! Upon check in our room was not ready, but they offered to hold our luggage and let us swim in their pool. The pool! It was a salt water pool on the 12th floor that juts out over Main Street in Dallas. The service there was exceptional, the area was very clean and very well maintained. The concierge came and gave us our room key when our room was ready. The room was immaculate - superbly decorated, super clean, and there was a complimentary bottle of champagne for us, with truffles and a lovely note from the manager. The room was superb! Large, quiet, excellent! The room service was wonderful - the food was great, and the service was, again, exceptional. Stay here - it's expensive, but absolutely worth it - we plan on returning next anniversary!

Not only was the hotel incredible with an amazing room, but the service and amenities are top notch. I needed a late night pressing of my suit. Done, with no hassle. Upon leaving the hotel I received a call that I left a very expensive watch in the room safe and it was returned with full communication. These folks go out of their way to make your stay enjoyable and hassle free.

My husband & I stayed a night for his birthday. We really enjoyed it. The smell when you walked into the lobby was breathtaking...the fragrance was wonderful. The front desk staff was very nice and smiled. The valet was very courteous (but very expensive at $27 a night) We had the King room on the 6th floor. I loved the bathroom set up and the shower was huge, big enough for 4 couples (if you're into that sort of thing). The housekeeper knocked on each door and handed out complimentary chocolates and bags of ice. The doorman who brought up our bags also offered to bring us ice. They even offer a turndown service which includes Rose Petals on the bed. That night we visited the PM Lounge that's located in the basement of the hotel. It was more like a nightclub than a Lounge. It was very crowded, you could barely move, but the drinks were very good. We had fun and it was great to go to a club and not have to drive home.

I spent 2 nights in the St. Regis in Houston prior to coming to this hotel. The Joule is not luxurious in comparison and not sure why Starwood has it branded as such. This is a W Hotel wanna-be for the over 40 set. The rooms are tiny and open like most W's and the focus on being trendy, not on customer service nor amenities. Designer soap in the bathroom does not a luxury hotel make. This hotel has a very cramped feel. Be warned, the building next door is under construction (which I am sure is temporary). It is clear this hotel has no loading dock or alley because while I was eating dinner at the award winning restaurant downstairs (Charlie Palmer's) I had big trucks pulling up within 10 ft of my table loading and unloading big crates of towels (I learned they outsource their linens) and other large pieces of equipment. It really ruined the experience for me. The pool was nice as was the fitness center but with tiny cramped rooms, lack of customer service (I tried calling the desk 3 times and never go through) and the loading dock at the front of the building, I wouldn't recommend it.

Great hotel interiors, dark moody decor in rooms. We stayed in a Junior Suite and it was well equipped. The actual floor space is less than other hotels, but still sufficient. Having said at, the bathroom was big, and really nice. Dark and moody still. The concierge was very helpful with organizing assistance and cars etc, by email before we arrived. The actual service at the front desk seemed a bit patchy, depending on who was there. The staff for the cars, porters and in the pool bar were all friendly and helpful. The guys dropped us at some shops, and also organized the rides too and from the hotel (with an external provider you pay direct). Overall, the hotel is good value for money, in the higher end range.

Went to Joule for anniversary get-away. Brand new hotel which is nice since so many hotels do not update once they are a little older. Very contemporary hotel but classy. We considered Ritz and Mansion on Turtle Creek but happily choice Joule. Service is hit or miss. They had free bottle of wine and chocolates in our room for our anniversary which was nice but I had to ask 3 times for ice bucket (it is small hotel so there are no ice machines on the floors). When I checked out they double billed for the room (once in my name and once in my wife's) and the guy at desk said they had had problems with that happening. There is Charlie Palmer restaurant in hotel but is not owned by hotel. Charlie Palmer cooks the room service menu but it is different menu than restaurant and didn't look as good (no foie gras). We ordered take out from Charlie Palmer and they even provided us plates and silverware. This was nice because we got the food we wanted, didn't have to worry about it being cold and got to watch UT kick Missouri's [----]. Location is in middle of downtown but lots of activities close by. Check out Iron Cactus for a drink - they have 3rd story rooftop bar that is really nice if weather is good. Also for the ladies one of Dallas' best spas (Sedona - lady's only) is across the street but make sure and get appointment in advance as my wife couldn't get same day appointment on Saturday. The hotel can arrange for in room or couples massage from Sedona. Also try brunch at Bread Winner's Cafe - just a short 3 miles away. We had dinner at Nobu which is in Crescent Court which was really good too.

query: hotel staff service friendliness and responsiveness

reviews.text: This is a great hotel to visit. The staff for the most part are excellent and helpful. For the most part the staff doesnt have all the attitude that the W staff does. Some of the younger front desk staff tend to be a little snooty. but for the most part, the staff is excellent. The concierge is very helpful and knows his stuff. The manager of the attached restaurantis also really helpful and provides excellent service - even though the restaurant is independently managed. The rooms are awesome except for the lack of privacy in the toilets that others have mentioned. The view from the lower floors is kinda cruddy and the street noise might get loud on the weekend. Overall, can't wait to come back.

Cons: Service is terrible!! Maybe I just had a bad experience but I was throughly disappointed in this hotel. It seemed as if they had the "summer staff" on duty. The valet just stood right next to me while I struggled with my luggage. He did not offer to help in any way. Once I was at the desk, I still was not offered any help with getting all my luggage to my room. That evening, I placed my room service order on my door well before the requested time of midnight. I only ordered a pot of coffee for 7am. After waiting 45 minutes, I finally opened my door and realized they didn't even pick up the card. It was still hanging on the door handle. After calling down to the desk, they did not even give a simple apology. Maybe I'm just spoiled, but I travel frequently and I have never recieved such poor service from an "upscale" hotel. Pros: The rooms were very clean and nice. I did have breakfast at the restaurant and the food was great. The service I recieved at the restaurant was also wonderful. They were prompt, polite, and very accomodating.

I travel at least once a month for work, and I was fortunate enough to stay at this hotel last February and it's such a charming hotel. The staff are courteous and professional, without overdoing it. The design and decor is incredible. The have really nice turn down service, too. The hotel and guest rooms are cozy without feeling too small. I would never hesitate to return to this hotel. I hope to be back.

Working with this hotel has been a breeze. Jessica and Byron were able to help organize my large group of 21 guests with ease. Every detail was managed perfectly. I am very happy with my stay. Thank you so much! Also, the hotel offers complimentary shoe shining service. -- LB

Stayed there for one night so I did not get to use any of the hotel services nor dine there. However, the staff were all very nice and helpful. They also have complimentary car service via a Cadillac Escalade which takes you and picks you up anywhere within 5 miles of the hotel. Truly a wonderful, and from my experience unique service. Being it is very contemporary, be prepared for glass shower and toilet doors. Bed was very plush and comfortable.

I live in the north DFW area, and it is my job to become very famiilar with many hotels and their services around the Metro-plex. The Joule was a refreshing experience and definitely a cut above the rest. Once I arrived, Danielle took great care to check me in and point me in the direction of my room, which I didn't leave much unless it was to have a meeting downstairs in the restaurant. Also, I must admit I took the liberty of telling alot of my friends about the beautiful pool that I had an hour to indulge in! It's not often I can say that I was treated like a celebrity. Craig respected my need for adhearance to a timely schedule during my check out and made it a seamless transaction. The decor, overall atmosphere, and excellent service in this hotel exceeds expectation. I would recommend this hotel to my existing and future out of town business clients when they visit, and I plan to make this my home away from home while conducting such visits. Thank you for renewing my faith in the hotel industry!

Trip to this hotel started off VERY poorly with a bungled reservation. I was so livid with how it was being handled that I was ready to completely lose it. However, Shawn at the bar, Scott the restaurant's executive chef, and Todd at the hotel bar have MORE than made up for the rough start. Their understanding of customer service, above and beyond attention to detail and courtesy have made this a repeat destination on the list. As a famous restaurant critic once said, "I'll forgive a bad meal but not bad service". Thank you Shawn, Scott, and Todd for more than making up for the beginning of this trip!

My very good friend booked a room at the Joule for her birthday last weekend and invited a few friends, myself included, to celebrate a safe and enjoyable evening. We began the evening in the hotel room, then walked a short distance to a nearby resturant for dinner. When we returned, we waited in line to enter the PM Lounge, a club on the bottom floor of the Joule. The doorman refused to allow us entry and we ended up waiting for almost an hour in the Texas heat while other folks would simply walk off the street and were immediately allowed in! My friend finally asked why we were waiting while everyone else was allowed in and the man very rudely announced that those folks were hotel guests. The birthday girl informed the man that she too was a hotel guest but he only said he would look into it. I was appalled that we were treated that way. The birthday girl waited for another 45 mins to speak to the hotel manager about the situation, but he was preoccupied trying to iron out a situation for some honeymooners who had made reservations that the hotel couldn't locate. (Apparently we weren't the only guests to have their evening botched by this hotel). After such a long and sweltering wait, the b-day girl's guests began to just leave out of frustration. The guest who remained were forced to go across the street to a dive bar where the b-day girl began to cry uncontrollably over her ruined special evening. It was insulting that the doorman/management were so disrespectful and unwilling to take care of their guest. I would never recommend this hotel or their club PM Lounge.

I stayed at The Joule for an extended amount of time throughout the summer. When deciding on where to stay for my training I was looking for a clean, upper scale hotel with exceptional service. Well, I picked the right one. EVERYONE I met there was extraordinarily nice to me. Some of the few that stand out would be Danielle, Jessica, and Katie at the front desk. Also Brendan and Craig were the best, they would bend over backwards to accommodate me. I would recommend this hotel to anyone; it is clean, luxurious and has out of this world service. - Mr. Ray

We stayed here for an Anniversary weekend getaway in Dallas and we were very impressed with the rooms and the service! We were treated to excellent service, including some perks at Charlie Palmer's and PM Lounge. I could not have had a more relaxing anniversary weekend. Front desk even followed up to see how everything was going with our stay. They also have an Escalade car service to take you to dinner reservations or anywhere within (I think) 5 miles of the hotel. Even with it being first come, first serve, the service only had about a 10 minute wait on a Saturday night. The room details were well thought out. Although the room we were in was a bit small, they had really nice decor and details that you would not see a Marriott or a Hilton, IMHO. The photos were interesting, the bathrooms unique, and the bed was really comfortable. It was essentially a "funky" modern look that suited us great. The only drawback was that the room faced a dilapidated building next door and they were doing construction on that side to extend the hotel (no construction noise on the weekend, just a view of the construction and rundown building!). Valet was pricey, but much preferred over worrying about my car in one of the nearby parking lots overnight. I will hopefully be back -- as the revitalized Main St. has a lot of action on the weekends and this hotel sits right in the middle! BTW, the pool and PM Lounge are really cool!

The staff here is great. I was there for 3 nights. it is always great when the doormen remember your name. I left a personal item behind when i checked out, and they called me that night and shipped it the next day. Wish the weather had been nice enough to use the pool.

I often stay at great hotels, but the staff at the Joule Hotel made our stay awesome beyond belief!!! Nicole, Nikki,maverick, Todd, and Andrew made our stay memorable! I'm so grateful for they're amazing service!!! When in Dallas stay Here!! !

I had a group of 18 for me and my coworkers here for a series of business meetings in Dallas. The hotel was beautiful; the staff was very accommodating; and it was very easy working with a large group. The only downside was that I was there in January, and the Poule was not open. I definitely will try to get back when it is warmer!

The hotel can arrange for in room or couples massage from Sedona. Also try brunch at Bread Winner's Cafe - just a short 3 miles away. We had dinner at Nobu which is in Crescent Court which was really good too.

Well it started off BAD within 10 mins we had went to the pool where we find about 5 young ladies workin and just stood there looking like we where not even there, so I was like excuse me can I get a drink. After my first drink we had to flag down a girl to ask for another as the pool area was not busy maybe 6 other people so ni reason for service to be that bad. Then I went up to bar to close tab again just standing there it took ten mins, then the manager of the pool and club pm was there and was very friendly offered us free drinks and help but I rejected I no longer wanted to be around that. This hotel does not have ice machines you have to call for ice well we called so we could have our own drink in room well lets say it NEVER CAME!!!! That evening we went down to the club PM which is in hotel very unfriendly and it took us for ever to get in and if your staying at hotel it is suppose to not be a problem to get in YEAH RIGHT!!!! ok Saturday we ate at Charlie Palmers resturant in hotel food was good but service was so bad I could get better service at MC Donalds than this supper bad. Then Saturday evening after having night of fun on town came back to order room service it took 45 mins. to get ONE sandwhich I had to call and ck on it and there are slow and the service is so bad and the managers know which makes it WORSE... Please do not waste ur money go to ZAZAS, The W, or the Ritz

Not only is this a great hotel, but I was traveling on business and experienced an illness during my trip. Not only did the hotel help me find a local doctor, but the manager on duty checked on me and sent chicken soup to the room to help me feel better. I wish i did not have to cut my trip short, because the pool looked like a lot of fun.

I read the reviews before I went so I addressed some of the service issues beforehand. My boyfriend and I stayed there for his birthday and I wanted everything to be perfect. Jessica, the front desk manager, was great. Their new GM is aware of the service issues they have had and he is working to turn it around. We were treated very well. They had a bottle of champagne,yummy chocolates and a cheese platter in the room. We stayed in one of the lofts and initially had some temperature issues but they were addressed quickly. The room was fantastic. Well decorated, sleek and modern. They have the top of the line Beautyrest mattress which was really comfortable. Two of the three bathrooms had huge walk in showers and double showerheads. The owner is an art collector so the lobby was decorated with pieces from his own personal collection. There is a sustainable energy theme in the hotel and Jessica and Brandon gave us the background story. If you go ask the front desk about it. Charlie Palmers is connected to the hotel and it is excellent. The sommelier at Charlie Palmers, Brandon was awesome. He coordinated with NOKA Chocolates for a private wine and chocolate pairing on Saturday afternoon. The pool area was packed and we had a cabana reserved for us. The pool is small but they keep it very cool and refreshing. It had a mini-Vegas poolside vibe. Their nightclub, PM, manages the pool area. We had opportunity to go to PM that night as well. We got the red carpet treatment. They had initially reserved us a table but when we got there it had been given away. They apologized profusely and comped us all our drinks. I would say that this place is worth a chance despite the reviews. The staff seems very willing to hear feedback and make it better. We had a lovely, relaxing weekend.

i had a business conference in Dallas and was fortunate enough to get a discounted rate at the Joule for myself and a few colleagues. our contact at the hotel, Jessica Craycraft, went above and beyond to provide us with quality service and was always available whenever we needed something. The staff was friendly yet very professional. the overall service provided was great value for money. the stay was a breeze. would love to go back i a heartbeat. the hotel has an excellent in house restaurant with plenty on the menu and delectable choices.

I am local to the area and on the recommendation of a co-worker, i stayed at the Joule instead of Zaza. From the minute I pulled into the hotel, it was nothing but first class service and a professional knowledgable staff. We ate at the restaurant before we were going to go out and the food was amazing and the service was second to none. I know that from Jennifer that checked us in with her welcoming smile we would have a good time. Craig is a knowledge person of the area and helped so much with all of our questions. I will be back again and recommend the switch to all my friends. Zaza is out and the Joule is the place to be

We have set up many group stays with The Joule and have always been very satisfied! Our contact, Jessica Craycraft, is very professional and is always eager to assist with our requests. Our guests are typically on the younger side, but everyone at the hotel has always treated them with the utmost of respect. The warm, modern feel of the hotel is a big hit with our guests! They also love the pool area that overlooks Main street! I would defintely recommend The Joule for group stays!

query: hotel room cleanliness and bathroom hygiene

reviews.text: The hotel was under exterior renovations, but that worked out for me as I was out of my room for most of the day. The rooms were completely renovated and tastefully done. The biggest issue is that upon going to bed the first night, I noticed an overpowering smell of urine in my bed. Stripping the sheets, I found a fairly fresh urine stain that made me want to vomit. Luckily, I retired the second bed in my room. I notified the front desk to make sure it was cleaned at some point. My gripe was that housekeeping must have noticed this when they changed the sheets, but made no attempt at cleaning the mattress and simply covered it back up. Some other minor issues were the desk chair in the room (it fell short of an appropriate working height of the desk and constantly fell down when your leg accidently hit the adjustment bar in front, poor choice of chairs), the elevator door was annoyingly slow to close (I was up and down several times per day), the exterior and lobby doors should be automatic and I noticed people struggling to open them and get their luggage through, they also were misaligned and did not open well. The wireless bill did not get charged to the bill, you had to enter your credit card for it. Never ever seen this in any hotel I have ever stayed at. Very annoying. Also, the restaurant downstairs I assummed is affiliated with the hotel, but the bill gave you no option to bill it to your room.

The hotel is in downtown Seattle right in the middle of it all. The Paramount theatre was across the street and there's shopping on every corner. Tiffany's was down the block. Pikes Market was 4 blocks away. The staff was very friendly and we're very accommodating. Tom in the lobby was very helpful with his suggestions on which tours to take to where to eat. The room was very clean. We asked for more towels and they arrived within minutes. There is an empty fridge for your use in the room, that was great. The first two days the person cleaning the room was excellent, the weekend shift was okay it was cleaned well but forgot to replace a robe, soap and the extra towels. The problems were rectified immediately. Would stay there again.

We've always enjoyed our stay at the Paramount Hotel in Portland, OR. So when family members were visiting us last month, we thought we'd spend a weekend with them at the Paramount in Seattle. The location was excellent (near downtown shopping as other reviewers have mentioned). Staff was very courteous and helpful. Compared to the Portland location, the Seattle Paramount needs some sprucing up. The elevator was marked and scuffed. The hallway to our room smelled of cleaning or toiletry products (we couldn't tell which). There appeared to be some water damage in our bathroom. However, our room was clean and quiet. It was a convenient location, but not a luxurious accomodation.

I stayed one night in the Paramount in room 315..Buyer beware, do not stay in this room as it overlooks the back parking lot over the Huge garbage dump..Also, faces the vents from the Chinese Restaurant attached to the hotel so the room is filled with the smell of frying foods(horrible) and garbage....Even if your window(small) is closed and the a/c on, the smell overwhelms ! Also, huge light is right outside window and shines very bright into the room. Otherwise, the Hotel is in a good location for sightseeing and shopping..

I did not enjoy my stay here. If you are on a budget and the other hotels are too pricy - Fairmont, etc - then this will work for you. But I thought the staff were unprofessional and I was uncomfortable with the men at the desk. I was put in a room that just didn't have the feeling be being fresh and clean. It was dark, dirty, and noisy from the construction right outside my window. The only food available is from a Chinese restaurant that is in the hotel. I didn't try it, but it doesn't look appetizing. Based on my overall experience I could not recommend this hotel.

i was happily surprised at the paramount hotel. first off, the location is stellar. easy 8 block walk to pike place market. the lobby is sort of lackluster but the rooms were tasfully updated and very clean. we asked and were granted an upgrade to a corner king executive which was pretty spacious. the beds were comfy and nice bathroom ammentities. only thing i did notice was in the hallways, as soon as you exited the elevator there was an odd smell but once you got inside your room it was gone. i would definitely stay here again.

The hotel was well designed and tastefully decorated. The room was large with a desk area, comfortable chairs and a very comfortable bed. The bathroom was roomy and supplied with great amenities. The hotel is in the downtown area and we were able to take the light rail from the airport, which was very helpful. It is within easy walking distance of shopping, great restaurants and Pike's Place. It is perfect for a couples get-away or a business trip. There is a good restaurant connected to the hotel. The personnel were very helpful and pleasant.

Ok, it is bad. The room is shabby, the shower made a horrible noise whenever the water was running. Sounded like a jackhammer. Valet parking was terrible. Did not want to leave our car there. Tons of construction in the neighborhood which starts at 6:30 am. Staff was rude and impatient. The location isn't even that good, a little to far north for me. A long walk back up hill from Pike Place Market to the hotel. And the price was too high for the quality of hotel and service. Live and learn.Booked our hotel before reading reviews on Trip Advisor.

Don't take a room on the inside unless you want to be awakened by the garbage trucks at 5am. The air conditioning vent had so much filthy residue trapped inside that it could not possibly pass a health audit. I stayed for 5 nights and by the 5th night I was dreadfully ill. I cannot say for sure that it was due to the room but it is highly suspect. My desk chair was broken and I asked for it to be replaced or fixed. They never did it. I would not advise you to stay here even if you think you have a great price. No breakfast no restaurant except an attached Asian food restaurant. Which was OK by the way for dinner.

Staid here during Sakura-Con with a group of teens. The front staff were not well versed in the local area. Trying to ask where restaurants were, the mall, transit. However, the bell man was kind and helpful. He was an older gentleman and I wish I would have gotten his name. When he saw I was getting no where with the front staff he came over and helped us out. The rooms for the price were not very good. The bathroom is the size of a closet and the hot water took forever to warm up. The halls had a very odd smell, like a dental office. You have to give a $50 daily deposit in case you use room service etc. Which they don't tell you when you reserve the room and I wasn't expecting. And all the other hotels I've ever stayed at (many) never had this. The location is great, right close to the convention center but other than for the bell man I wouldn't recommend this place. There are plenty of other hotels and we will be trying a different one for the convention next year.

My wife, one year-old son and I stayed at the Paramount for two nights over a weekend to attend a family wedding at the Hyatt across the street. The location is great (ten minute walk from Pike Place Market) but construction in and around the area means you're forced to use valet parking ($25/night). Our first day and night at the hotel were great. Room is decent and clean. The cleaning staff is very friendly; the frontdesk staff and valets are OK. The in-house restaurant is mediocre but not too pricey. Things started to go terribly wrong on our second night. Our toliet overflowed at 11pm resulting in a flood in our bathroom. A cleaning staff person caming to our room and plunged the toilet, but the toilet plugged up again the next morning. This time a real maintenance person came and fixed it, but noone came to clean the floor like we requested. The manager knocked off $50 for that incident. We then called down to have our car retrieved from the valet upon checking out. They could not find our car for about an hour! We nearly thought our car was stolen! Still not sure why our car could not be found for that time. Meanwhile our son was tearing up the lobby. Needless to say we left the hotel very frustrated and upset. We found out afterwards that the manager took off the second night room charge and parking from the bill, but the damage has been done. Even though rates are half that of the Hyatt, maybe go to a better hotel with better service.

Stayed at The Paramount in late September 2011 for one night before a cruise. Got a pretty good deal on Priceline by doing my own bid. Much better than the regular rates of the hotel website or any other travel booking engine. The lobby is small, but nice. The desk clerk was very friendly and efficient and was willing to help in answering any questions. Had a room on the 8th floor facing The Grand Hyatt. The room was clean and the beds were fine. You can't expect much better from a 3 star hotel. I don't like the shampoo and conditioner dispenser attached to the wall in the shower though. They just seem unsanitary to me. I far rather prefer the individual bottles. It was a south facing room and in the sun, tended to get a little hot. The A/C, no matter how low it was set, didn't keep the room very cool. May be just a problem with that room and wasn't a big issue only being there for the one night. The room-service was way overpriced for mediocre food though. Hotels in Seattle tend to be very expensive, especially downtown. The location was great. Right across the street from Ruth's Chris Steak House and the Grand Hyatt. Only one block walk to the Nordstrom flagship store, three blocks to Macy's and about six to Pike Place Market. The valet man was excellent. He ran two blocks down to get us a cab to the cruise terminal. He got a nice tip for that. I'd stay here again for the right price, but I wouldn't pay the full fare.

We were very impressed with what we got for the price we paid. The hotel is recently remodeled and the rooms are very clean and modern as is the hotel lobby. The location is excellent being just a short walk to Pike Place and various neighborhoods for shopping and dining. The restaurant is excellent - with 7 hours of happy hour specials a day - who could argue?! The only thing keeping this from being a 5 star review all the way around is that we could hear the person in the next room peeing. Not the most romantic thing to hear as you're lying in bed. Other than the thin wall between rooms, it was an excellent stay and we'd definitely stay there again.

This is a very nice hotel. Our king-size bed was very comfortable. The room was very clean and anything you may need was available in the room. It was very quiet. There was some city traffic noise but not noticable. After a long day of sightseeing it was great to come back to. Our only complaint was the cost of parking our car. I wish we would've not rented a car and took the train from the airport. There is so much to see in Seattle and great free transportation.

Reading some reviews after staying for a week in late September prompted me to add my review; I think some of the unhappy reviewers need to do their research better before booking a hotel so as not to blame the hotel for their own lack of knowledge. I researched heavily for my first stay in Seattle and one of many to come since my son now lives in Seattle. I must say I had no significant complaint at all with this hotel during the entire week staying there. The worst I can come up with is hearing the neighbors thru the adjoining door occasionally. The best included the cleanliness, the attention to detail with lighting and electrical outlets, the comfortable furniture, the robes, the great shower, the refrigerator, the windows can open, the wide and well lit hallways (although too warm) and of course an excellent king bed. The restaurant was always convenient for a quick happy hour and even allowed me to take a drink or a dessert upstairs; the concierge went out to the store to deliver me a Sunday NY Times newspaper. There is a great coffee shop across the street and the stunning Paramount Theater down the block. Of course, walking downtown was easy. I will be very happy to stay at this hotel each time I return to Seattle, especially if I can get the great rate I paid by calling the hotel directly to book in advance. Paramount, you were outstanding for what you promised to be.

We booked the Paramount with a little apprehension, since downtown hotels are often either industrial/impersonal or old school fusty. The Paramount was neither, rather a tastefully designed, conveniently located (close to all central attractions and within the Ride Free Area for public transportation) facility. Our room had a new and contemporary feel. The bathroom was indeed on the small side but it presented no problems. Service from the desk staff and the bellman was totally helpful, anything we asked was "no problem." We encountered no advance charges for room service or damage; hopefully that policy is gone. Now, a few drawbacks - the hotel charges $9.95/day for wifi, does any other motel/hotel anywhere do that anymore? There are 2 free computers in the lobby, so it wasn't a major problem for us, but it's a bad policy. Parking is all valet and $27/day. I guess that's standard practice in downtown hotels, but it really makes it cumbersome to get the car. Luckily, as I said, for our 1 night there it wasn't a big issue.

I am writing this review from my room at the Paramount, actually, and I have been very pleased with the hotel during my stay this week. The location is within a reasonable walking distance of shopping, restaurants, and the Pike Place Market (if you pack the proper shoes!). The neighborhood feels comfortable and safe to me, which is important as a female traveling alone. The lobby is warm and cozy with couches and a fireplace. The room is well-appointed with contemporary furnishings and a comfortable bed. There's a big TV, a sleek marble bathroom, a small closet, and a large desk in the room. I stayed at the Warwick on my previous trip, and I've found the Paramount so much more to my liking. I will absolutely stay here again if given the option. And I've already recommended it to my fellow coworkers for their future trips to our corporate HQ. Things I don't love about the Paramount: The view isn't much --- the rooms look toward other high-rise buildings. The pillows are all really firm. The don't match the soft coziness of the bedding or mattress. They're like cuddling up with couch cushions. It would be nice to have an in-room microwave. There IS a mini-fridge, but no microwave if you want to use that mini-fridge to store leftovers. Your only option for room service (aside from breakfast) is overpriced -- tasty, but overpriced -- Asian cuisine from Dragonfish. The room service order-taker and delivery person were both very nice and professional, but it would be wonderful to have a wider range of menu options to select from.

I couldn't get the Grand Hyatt across the street to guarantee a room with two beds for the weekend I wanted earlier this month, so I picked the Paramount instead. Pros: 1- Quick service. This is a small place and they react quickly. I had a problem with the knob on my shower the first morning and I had maintenance at my door within 5 minutes to fix it so I could get on the move. After I left I had a tiny billing error on my corporate card and John fixed it over the phone with no problems or hassle. 2- Smart layout. This is not a huge corporate hotel. Its very good for no nonsense travelers like myself. The lobby has a nice little living room style waiting area but only takes 10 seconds to get through to the elevators. There's free internet tucked away to the side of the check in desk. The rooms are stylish and the bathrooms give you privacy if you are staying with someone else ( no peekaboo showers or open tops like some of the boutique hotels are pushing.) The windows open also if you want fresh air (big plus for me!) 3- Location. Pine Street is much easier to walk down to the Market than some of the other downtown streets (less incline.) Lots of shopping and restaurants within 2 - 3 blocks. Barnes and Noble right on the corner. Monorail super close. Bartell's drugstore with trial size toiletries next to Nordstroms. The downtowner shuttle also drops off within a block of the hotel and the new light rail to Seatac has a stop right on Pine at one of the malls. Cons 1- No view really. I looked out at the gray monolith walls of the Grand Hyatt. All in all a good stay. If you don't need all of the bells and whistles but still like a little style to your room, I would recommend this place. It did the job.

We recently stayed at this hotel during our Canada/USA holiday. This hotel was beautiful. Large room, with amazing king size bed, stunning bathroom, and a view. We were sad that we didnt get to stay longer at this hotel. Great location, we walked to Pike Market and further. There was transport close by, and some great shops/restaurants. Staff were really helpful. We would recommend this hotel without hesitation.

Just came back and loved this hotel. Newly renovated rooms with high-end fixtures. The rooms were quite stunning. I believe we had a basic room with 2 queen beds and it was really lovely. Nice little bar fridge, very comfy beds with white duvets (I hate hotel bedspreads!). Location was amazing with 2 movie theatres (our bellman went down and printed off the movie listings from their computer and brought them back to our room) and markets easily walkable. The Dragonfish Sushi is right in the hotel downstairs. It was fantastic and has great deals and specials. I had Sake for $1. Check their website.

query: hotel staff service friendliness and responsiveness

reviews.text: The hotel since I last stayed had gone through a nice renovation. But the service I got from the staff at different times of the day was like day and night. During the morning Tom is more than willing to the extra mile to make sure you ready for your travels around the city, Jerry who works at the front desk also very helpful, nice and courteous. I will admit I made alot of requests and each time he was more than obliged to make sure it was taken care of. Lolita was great as well. Now on to the bad, the other staff. The man who was working at the front desk looked very gruff and mean, when I would ask something he made me feel like I was putting him out. He also looked very unprofessional as he was unshaven and failed to smile during my time there. The other fellow named Rich was very aloof , didnt know anything and confusing. Restaurant staff was also very poor

This hotel is probably one of the best in terms of location for shopping and restaurant etc. but the staff are a bit clueless. Every time I called down to the Front Desk with questions it felt like I was putting them out. Their tone of voice was no better than a 13 year old with a bad attitude! Not to mention when I checked in they yelled my room number out to me, not a good idea as a female travelling alone... The back breaker was when I called the concierge asking what time the mariners game started that day as I had tickets, he told me 7pm. When I got there at 7pm the game had been on for one hour as it started at 6:05!! Pretty basic information for a concierge to screw up on! When I had got back to my room the first day I was there housekeeping had still not been to my room, I had left at 9am and it was then 3:30. I called down to the front desk to find out what time housekeeping would be coming by as I wanted to have a nap before I went to the game. Their answer was they can come now or not at all as they leave at 5pm, how that was my problem I am not sure as they had all day to clean it... The restaurant was great, the service alright... The food was awesome and the prices are pretty good. Over all I would probably only stay here again based on location alone, it would have to be a good deal as well or I would stay at the Vintage Park or Pacific Plaza hotel.

The hotel was well designed and tastefully decorated. The room was large with a desk area, comfortable chairs and a very comfortable bed. The bathroom was roomy and supplied with great amenities. The hotel is in the downtown area and we were able to take the light rail from the airport, which was very helpful. It is within easy walking distance of shopping, great restaurants and Pike's Place. It is perfect for a couples get-away or a business trip. There is a good restaurant connected to the hotel. The personnel were very helpful and pleasant.

I was booked into this hotel for business. The staff is friendly and very helpful. The hotel was recently renovated and is really nice. The rooms were clean and I forgot an item and was able to get it back from the front desk staff. DragonFish, the restaurant downstairs was good too. I highly recommend it if staying downtown in Seattle.

I did not enjoy my stay here. If you are on a budget and the other hotels are too pricy - Fairmont, etc - then this will work for you. But I thought the staff were unprofessional and I was uncomfortable with the men at the desk. I was put in a room that just didn't have the feeling be being fresh and clean. It was dark, dirty, and noisy from the construction right outside my window. The only food available is from a Chinese restaurant that is in the hotel. I didn't try it, but it doesn't look appetizing. Based on my overall experience I could not recommend this hotel.

Laid back, nonintrusive hotel suitable for business or vacation stays, centrally located on Pine--3 blocks from Westlake, a block from the bus terminal ($2.75 airport transfers), and a block from Von's Martini and Manhattan Shrine, never to be missed. Off-lobby sushi restaurant also serves conventional breakfast, lively at night. But walking over to Pike and up a couple blocks, you're at Tango, never to be missed on any trip to Seattle. The rooms are pleasant and clean, with the baffling omission of a coffee maker or kettle--really a weird thing to forget. Instead of a mini-bar, there's a small refrigerator with two bottles of $2.50 water--drink from the tap instead. Complete personal care from 40-year veteran, bell captain Tom Fleege, a happy and gracious individual who has been a fixture on this corner at the former Camlin Hotel across the street. If you have the interest, chat him up--this is a modest man who has really distinguished himself in the conduct of his life. He is the soul of the hotel, which is not to take anything away from his colleague, Richard, or the elegant and helpful John Hiles at the front desk. This is a well-run place. Not counting the missing kettle! At the last minute, we booked a conference room for a couple days. Excellent service from the restaurant, asinine charges from AT&T for the wireless, but what do you expect.

Across the street from the Paramount Theater, and down the street from Pacific Place and Westlake Mall, this hotel offers a great location for tourists wanting to stay in town to be close to all that's going on, as well as for residents that are looking for a weekend of culture or shopping in the city. The staff is gracious and welcoming, responds to requests and questions in a helpful manner, and seem to genuinely care that you enjoy your stay in their hotel and your visit to the city. Rooms are roomy, especially by many downtown standards, and come nicely appointed with newly updated furniture and linens. The flat screen television is perfect for a late night movie or watching the morning news. Lots of plugins (including two pop up plugs in on each of the nightstands) mean this is gadget friendly. Wi-fi, however, was spotty in strength, and I frequently had difficulty maintaining a connection. The hotel relies on a third party (Wayport) to provide service.

At midnight the attendant could not find my reservation, even though I provided a confirmation number. He had me wait for an hour while he assisted other guests. He was very rude and would not let me use the phone to call other hotels for vacancies. Later the manager offered me a night in one of their associated hotels; another wild goose chase with unreturned calls and false promises. PLEASE don't give this awful chain your business!

was back at this hotel after a couple years and I would like to point out that Jerry who is the reservation or front desk manager has been a welcome constant at this hotel, made my reservation through him and was also checked in as well by him. He is nice and was very helpful. The hotel has gone through some renovations which make it look nice, Dragonfish changed their menu a bit but their food is still good. A nice and elegant no frills hotel with great personal service, I have and always will recommend this hotel. Ask for Jerry he will take care of you.

Ok, it is bad. The room is shabby, the shower made a horrible noise whenever the water was running. Sounded like a jackhammer. Valet parking was terrible. Did not want to leave our car there. Tons of construction in the neighborhood which starts at 6:30 am. Staff was rude and impatient. The location isn't even that good, a little to far north for me. A long walk back up hill from Pike Place Market to the hotel. And the price was too high for the quality of hotel and service. Live and learn.Booked our hotel before reading reviews on Trip Advisor.

The hotel is in downtown Seattle right in the middle of it all. The Paramount theatre was across the street and there's shopping on every corner. Tiffany's was down the block. Pikes Market was 4 blocks away. The staff was very friendly and we're very accommodating. Tom in the lobby was very helpful with his suggestions on which tours to take to where to eat. The room was very clean. We asked for more towels and they arrived within minutes. There is an empty fridge for your use in the room, that was great. The first two days the person cleaning the room was excellent, the weekend shift was okay it was cleaned well but forgot to replace a robe, soap and the extra towels. The problems were rectified immediately. Would stay there again.

Amazing motel, amazing staff. Loved the pillowtop beds, beautiful rooms, very quiet. Big screen TV, refrigerator, coffee pot, all added to comfort. Squeaky clean room and nice size. We enjoyed dining at the Dragonfish restaurant for great food and reasonable pricing. Felt right at home and appreciated secure valet parking. Assistance is all around w/ staff waiting to help on all levels. Very close to all downtown shopping and exploring. It was a wonderful hotel, but not intimidating or snobbish. Generally, when we stay at a downtown Seattle hotel, we are happy to be getting back to our own homes and beds, but with Paramount, we were sorry we didn't have a few more days. It was that comfortable and amazing. Will definitely be booking with Paramount again soon.

Reading some reviews after staying for a week in late September prompted me to add my review; I think some of the unhappy reviewers need to do their research better before booking a hotel so as not to blame the hotel for their own lack of knowledge. I researched heavily for my first stay in Seattle and one of many to come since my son now lives in Seattle. I must say I had no significant complaint at all with this hotel during the entire week staying there. The worst I can come up with is hearing the neighbors thru the adjoining door occasionally. The best included the cleanliness, the attention to detail with lighting and electrical outlets, the comfortable furniture, the robes, the great shower, the refrigerator, the windows can open, the wide and well lit hallways (although too warm) and of course an excellent king bed. The restaurant was always convenient for a quick happy hour and even allowed me to take a drink or a dessert upstairs; the concierge went out to the store to deliver me a Sunday NY Times newspaper. There is a great coffee shop across the street and the stunning Paramount Theater down the block. Of course, walking downtown was easy. I will be very happy to stay at this hotel each time I return to Seattle, especially if I can get the great rate I paid by calling the hotel directly to book in advance. Paramount, you were outstanding for what you promised to be.

Stayed here for 3 nights with my best friend recently. The hotel is just great! The staff is friendly and super helpful (ie: tourist questions, room questions etc), the rooms are neat and clean and comfortable, the location is perfect and close to everything you need downtown including transit to anything outside of downtown (monorail, bus stops, lightrail). We were also provided with free Wifi, which was great! I would definitely recommend this hotel as we had a fantastic experience with it!

Our aim was to get away for a few days, do some shopping and have a few good meals. The hotel was very well positioned to do that being central to all the major downtown stores and Pike Pklace Market. The hotel restaurant was no great shakes but it is walking distance to some great eateries. Would certainly return.

I stayed at the Paramount while I was at a major political science convention down the street at the Washington State Convention Center. The hotel is wonderfully situated for that--two blocks from the convention center entrance and across the street from another hotel where some of the conv. events were happening. The room was not huge but it was immaculately clean and very stylish. The bed was very comfortable and hot water was plentiful. With the exception of one clerk who wasn't a lot of help advising me on finding a cheap nearby breakfast (" I don't know--this IS Seattle...") the staff was unusually friendly and helpful, always welcoming me back when I came in. Far more smiles from the staff than the typical hotel, too. The area felt safe and it was walking distance to the light rail to the airport; I took some longer walks to Capital Hill, to an Episcopal church on Sunday morning and to the Pike Place market area several times--all were fun walks to take. I don't know when I'll be in Seattle again--it's a long way from Maine!--but when I do I would be happy to stay here again.

My family had a girl's weekend in Seattle and chose The Paramount Hotel due to it's proximity to all the attractions. We took the Link Light Rail and got off on the last stop (can't remember the name). The hotel was a short 2 block walk away. Very convenient when one does not want to hassle with a rental car. The hotel was in a great location within walking distance to all the major shopping and Pike's Place Market. Rooms were comfortable as far as size and also very quiet. Staff was pleasant. The only complaint I have about the hotel are the beds. They were were soft (as were the pillows) and didn't offer much support. I didn't have any aches or pains from the beds, but I have definitely experienced better in other hotels. Overall, I would suggest this to anyone going to Seattle needing to be near all the action!

I was in town for business and booked the hotel through my corporate travel agency. My rate was $142 a night which I found to be a great value. It was a great location and within walking distance to a lot of the tourist attractions and businesses. My room was clean. The front desk was very helpful, I had a 6:00 AM flight and they arranged for transport to the airport. The hotel restuarant, Dragonfish, was good. They had a happy hour every day with good drink and food prices. I would stay there again. Given the location and price, I would rate my stay as above average.

I stayed at the Paramount June 1-3 in conjunction with a trade show at the convention center. Great location for conventions and an easy walk into the heart of downtown. The room was OK, typical hotel room with queen bed, desk, TV, clock radio, coffee maker. My room was warm and I discovered the fan was on, but the A/C was not. The thermostat was worn so you could not tell which setting was A/C and which was heat. It was sunny and 85 degree temps; needed the a/c after hauling materials to/from the show. They use energy saving compact flourescent bulbs so the room was not very bright for reading. Definitely needed the curtains open by day. I found the front desk staff to be very helpful, though the bellman gave me incorrect info when I asked where I could find a DHL office. Ate dinner at Dragonfish, the restaurant that shares space with the hotel. They seemed to draw a local crowd as well as some hotel guests. Food and service were very good. I did not use room service. If you have a car, parking is $25 night. The trade show arranged a negotiated rate so I did not compare rates with other hotels in advance. My two night stay with parking and taxes was $389. Overall a good value for a downtown hotel in high season. Not fancy, but offered exactly what I needed.

This is a very nice hotel. Our king-size bed was very comfortable. The room was very clean and anything you may need was available in the room. It was very quiet. There was some city traffic noise but not noticable. After a long day of sightseeing it was great to come back to. Our only complaint was the cost of parking our car. I wish we would've not rented a car and took the train from the airport. There is so much to see in Seattle and great free transportation.

hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
query: hotel room cleanliness and bathroom hygiene

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: the hotel is centrally located and is very comfortable with a nice bed and rooms cleaned daily. The hotel however seems to be ageing with the air con unit making a loud grinding noise and shower water sometimes talking hours to drain from the bath tub due to a blockage. Overall, not perfect but good value for money. would stay again.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: I just want to add my comments here. I was just on a business trip and because of circumstances had to stay at the Primrose for one night before I came back to the States. It was gay pride week so very few rooms were available and I had to take a smoking room here at this God-awful place. I've stayed in many places around the world but this was the worst. You felt as if you needed a shower just being in the hotel. It is very worn and in a terrible area of town. Nothing in the room felt clean and I agree with one reviewer that the bed "crunched". I could not believe what they charged for a room at this hell-hole, and it is funny just around the corner from the building is a "back-packer's hostel which I thought would have been much better than this dump. Heed this warning stay away from this crappy place, you'll be glad you did.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: This was my second stay at the Best Western Primrose in the past year and I would have no hestitation in staying again. I booked a smoking room with a king-size bed. It was a business class room, which I didn't really need, but I had anticipated having someone else come along on this trip. The room also included a sofa bed. The room was spacious and clean with an extremely comfortable bed. Is the hotel showing signs of wear? Sure, it's not a new hotel. If I looked closely I could see where the wallpaper had been patched in a spot near the bed's headboard. It wasn't obvious and I only noticed it because I was accessing a wall plug behind the bedside table. The carpet could use replacing for staining, but it wasn't dirty, just old. The lobby was clean, as was the elevator. Checking in and out was very quick. The staff were friendly and efficient. The location is great. Close enough to walk to the Eaton Centre. Close to good restaurants. The subway station is only a few blocks away and the street car passes right in front of the hotel.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: What is wrong with people? This is a good hotel we had no problems with our stay or room. The room was clean there were no stains anywhere, nice bed and dÃ©cor was good. People stay in hotels and expect them to be newly decorated for them rooms have to be used and accommodating. We use many hotels and in our stays, at Best Westerns all over the world have not had a bad one in the chain. Reception staff were polite and respected us, if you give staff respect we always find they give respect back, if you treat staff without respect what do you expect in return? Even housekeeping spoke to us in a morning and passed the time of day. The porterage was efficient and the bell boys were polite. We stayed with a tour on 9/10 September and would have no hesitation at staying or recommending this hotel again. My partner has worked in hotels for over 30 years and a lot of it in management and he would know a bad one as soon as he walked in. We normally take pictures of the rooms we stay in but unforunately did not on this occassion, if had they would have been put on here good or bad.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: I booked the â€œPrimroseâ€� Best Western, downtown Toronto a few days ago for a trip that we had planned. We arrived at 3:00 in the morning, and drove through the night to arrive to the filthiest hotel we have ever seen! Not knowing much about hotels in Toronto, and trusting the name â€œBest Westernâ€�, we decided to save a few dollars and book online. While taking an elevator to our room, we noted the bottom of the elevator was being held together with a piece of plywood. Exhausted, we walked into our room, and experienced the most overwhelming foul smells, I canâ€™t even describe! My husband laughed when he saw the conditions of the bathroom. A bathtub so filthy I wouldnâ€™t dare stand to take a shower. Weâ€™ve travelled to some very poor countries in our lives, but weâ€™ve never seen such dirty conditions! The room was so filthy, we decided to leave, and find another hotel. We didnâ€™t realize that the Primrose Best Western hotel was in the middle of a large prostitution area, until we left and noticed the building was surrounded by dozens of prostitutes. When we arrived at the Hilton (which we really couldnâ€™t afford, but were tired and in desperate need of a clean place to stay), staff noted that â€œThe Primroseâ€� Best Western was know for their bedbugs!!! Sure enough, when we returned to Ottawa, a Google search revealed that they indeed they had bedbug problems years ago!!! I am a nurse from Ottawa, and basic cleanliness is my only must for a hotel. PLEASE, save yourself the bother, spend the extra few dollars, and go to a reputable hotel!!! Please see bedbugs: [--]

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: My friends and I decided to stay at this hotel for two nights because the price was so good. The hotel was dirty. The shower was disgusting and there were marks all over the walls and carpet. The hallways were also very dim and can be scary at night. The elevators took forever! Be prepared to wait at least five minutes, and the doors sensors do not work, which was very annoying. The staff treatment was alright. They weren't that friendly. I had called down to front desk to ask for some extra towels and they were giving me a hard time. We had also asked the concierge for directions to certain areas in Toronto and he wasn't helpful. I guess this hotel would be ok for people who are looking to party. I wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for a nice weekend getaway or a family looking for a vacation. Spend the extra money and stay somewhere clean with friendly service.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: This was one of the worst experiences I have ever with a hotel room that cost $160 a night. The elevators were very scary and one was constantly being repaired. When at the restaurant, they gave me catchup that was so rancid it bubbled. There was brown stuff on the walls of the bathroom, and the room was very shabby. It was either too hot or too cold. For $10 extra I could have stayed at the Sheraton!

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: This was my first time travelling to Toronto and I must say this hotel ruined it for me. I booked this hotel, because I expected a certain cleanliness that comes with Best Western franchise's. My first room had a window that would not close, so I did not have much time to look around, I went to the front desk and asked to have my room switched. The front desk operator made me feel like it was a nuicence for him to switch my room. My second room also had a window that would not close, there were beer caps scattered throughout the room, there was hair in the tub and on the toilet seat, and the room smelt like an ashtray. I would never ever stay at this hotel again, and may never stay at a best western again.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: I stayed at the Primrose for ten days and I did like the beds as well as the location of the hotel. Just a couple of blocks away from Yonge & Dundas Square. It is a great location to explore the city by foot. The room itself was spacious with a king size bed, a sofa, desk, coffee maker (which I did not use), and a chair. I would describe it as typical Best Western standard 3 star hotel quality, nothing special and no frills. What did bother me though was the cleanliness. I did speak to housekeeping and the reception but the somehow they managed not to get the room clean thoroughly. The dust built up in the bathroom and on the carpet was substantial, seriously dust bunnies. Also which was bothersome was the wifi. It was so slow it was practically useless. I did ask if I just could use maybe a land line but no luck.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: After reading several of the other reviews, I was apprehensive about staying there. The room was clean, and had a great view. The staff was friendly. The rooms are in need of a remodel. The bathrooms are dated. If you are looking for an expensive four or five star hotel, don't stay here. This hotel is near everything; subway, restaurants, shopping. It offers a good value and excellent location. I parked my car in the garage for two days and took the subway.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: My wife and I recently took a trip to Toronto for our 35th wedding anniversary and booked in at the Primrose Hotel. It was close to the theatre we were going to and the price was affordable. We were extremely impressed with both the hotel and the service. We mentioned on check in that it was our anniversary and were immediately upgraded from our room with 1 double to a king room on the highest floor with a wonderful view of the city. They were also kind enough to recommend and make reservations at a lovely restaurant called Ruth Chris (pricey but well worth it if you are a steak lover). The hotel was in a great location and we walked to a charming area called Yorkville. The room itself was very spacious and clean. I saw some work being done in the lobby and wonder if they also did the rooms as our furniture looked to be new and had no damage or wear you normally see. The only issue I did not like was that the fan in the bathroom automatically turns on when you turn on the light, and usually my wife likes to sleep with the bathroom light on, but we didnâ€™t as the fan would be running. Other than that, we were most pleased with the hotel and hope to return again on our 40th.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: We chose to stay here because our daughter was staying in the student accommodation here as well. It's only a two and a half star hotel so you can't expect all the luxuries of a 4 or 5 star and as a result it was well priced. The room had 2 double beds and was reasonably spacious. No fridge or electric jug but I think that is normal for a standard room in any hotel in North America. The beds were comfortable and the sheets good quality but the furniture is pretty dated and the bathroom very tired looking. It did have nice white towels and a good selection of toiletries. A four cup coffee maker and supplies and complementary wi-fi were useful. Â The carpet wasn't as well vacuumed as one would expect with the corners and edges not done for a while. The window looking at a fantastic view north was so grimy it was hard to see through (finger and nose prints all over it) We just kept the net curtains closed so we couldn't see them and enjoyed the night lights instead. We didn't complain as we had already made ourselves at home & strewn all our belongings around the room and it would have been a bother to move. The location is good being a short walk into town and is close to the new Loblaws food emporium at Maple Leaf Gardens.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: This was certainly not the greatest hotel I have ever stayed in. I picked it because it was three stars, had internet access, and was stumbling distance from the concert two of us were attending. I booked a single room with two beds for the four of us and it was acceptable. Well, with the exception of the bathroom. It was small and not very clean. The staff were rude and quite useless, they just seemed annoyed and unwilling to help no matter how polite we were. Which made it easy to stumble through the lobby drunk and singing at 1:00 a.m. There was a 'restaurant' that never did open the three days, two nights we stayed and no room service. None of the 'perks' of the hotel were available-pool, steam room, gym, and the TV was old and hardly worked. The room we payed for with internet access, didn't have internet access. They at least lent us an external wifi card but it still didn't work. And they never did give us any form of refund for that either. There were 'ladies of the night' out front of the hotel, but they were harmless and didn't hassle us at all. I had a great time, as did my other friend. But that was due to the amount of rum we consumed and an amazing concert. I don't feel our two friends enjoyed the stay as much as we did. I would not stay there again.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: I wan't expecting much from this hotel and that's what I got. The general feeling of this hotel was tired and run down. We had to switch rooms the first night due to plumbing issues (shower didn't work, toilet leaked). Only good thing was that it was a few blocks from the subway.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
