reviews.text: I am participating in the student residence program and my first thought was that it would be awsome living in a hotel. Well I was wrong. My room connects with another room and you can hear the neighbour's television blasting and their conversations. One night I had the unfortunateness of hearing my neighbour's "good time" if you get my drift. The food is god awful, my stomach had to get used to it. The laundry facilitys are in poor quality. There are only four washers and one is always "out of service". A woman at the front desk is the rudest person i have ever met. The elevators are super slow. I do not recomemnd taking the elevators in the morning if you are only a few flights from the main floor because people are sardined in the elevator please take the stairs. Also I think there is a private school also staying in the hotel because there are little kids in uniforms screaming about. The bathroom has mold on the ceiling and the toilet paper is like tissue paper. There are stains on my bed and it's literally sleeping on a gym mat in student residence. The room thermostat doesn't stay the same temperature. When you turn it down and gradually goes up and if you can sleep only when it's a cool temperature you are going to have to wake up in the middle of the night to turn down the thermostat again. So if you are coming to Primose hotel I would recommend coming during may through august because that's when all the college students and noise is gone. I think they should use the money that they have ripped off people and take some time to fix up their hotel. Also,if you are planing to stay here for student residence don't make it your first choice, please look around maybe stay in a dorm or something.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: I/we have stayed at the Primrose Hotel 2 â€“ 3 times. We choose the hotel for its proximity to the Gay Village in Toronto (Church and Wellesley area). It is handy to shopping and night life â€“ but so are many other hotels from which to choose. Each time weâ€™ve stayed I have always had the impression that the place needs a good cleaning. It was a little worn down at the edges and maybe has undergone a serious facelift since last we were there. Lord knows that it needed to be done. It appeared to be a well managed facility. Several of the rooms appeared to be rented by students, either from Ryerson or the National Ballet School, both of which are very close. The one good thing that came about from our stays at this hotel was finding The Golden Greek Restaurant which is in the lower part of the building next door. It is a small, friendly, family own/operated business. This restaurant has a loyal group of customers. As someone who visits maybe once every year they remember you â€“ canâ€™t beat that for customer service. The food they serve is good as well. As Iâ€™ve said in the past of other facilities, if you compare this hotel to others of similar value in the same general area, you would choose another establishment. We tried this hotel and will pass on it in the future.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: On the way up to my room - I got stuck in an elevator. This was a good indication of how my stay was going to be at the hotel. The rooms are old, the bathroom smelled, we had a view of air conditioners and the gym was a joke. No working treadmills and a couple of out of date machines. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone!

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: Regardless of being on the fringes of a very "colorful" community, there was one incident that soured our stay at the Primrose. We accidently left a piece of jewelry in the room. Despite our best efforts to convey how irreplaceable it was, housekeeping claimed not to have seen it. We are heartbroken and will never recommend this hotel to anyone.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: This is a decent hotel, but factor in the low prices, great location and little perks like free wi-fi, and I'd say that it's one of the best I've stayed in. Not a luxury hotel by any means, but great value for the price. The room was big, clean and quite nice, the bed was very comfortable, there was plenty of hot water... the basics were covered. I found the staff to be helpful and courteous as well. A few very minor complaints - the bathroom was very small and a bit cold, since the only heat was from a small baseboard heater. The TV had something wrong with it and made a loud buzzing noise the whole time it was on, but since I wasn't there to watch TV that wasn't a big deal. I didn't eat at the restaurant, so can't comment on that. Overall, a good experience and I would definitely stay there again.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: As other reviewers are saying, the place needs a facelift fast. Some hospitality training for the staff wouldn't be too much to ask either. A couple of my friends and I stayed there for a weekend of fun and it was awful from the start. Mind you, we were all college age guys, not too concerned about what the place looked like. But from the time they told us we had to go get public parking down the street, to mixed up room arrangement, through just rude service, and a tile falling from the bathroom wall, the price was not worth it. The only thing this place has going for it is the location close to the bars and clubs (which might be a minus if you don't want to risk running into prostitutes on your walk back from dinner). Reading some of the good reviews posted it seems we stayed at different hotels. But if you're thinking of staying at this one, pass it up.

hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
query: hotel staff service friendliness and responsiveness

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: My experience at this hotel was the worst I've ever experience within the service industry. It is obvious that Customer Service is not a priority for this hotel. All they want is money. The front desk is rude and inexperienced. Being from out of town, we drove to Toronto to spend a nice week-end. The first impression we got from the Primrose Best Western was rudeness. Before checking in, they rudely told us that the parking space we had requested had been given to someone else and that we were to go down the street to public parking lot. THEY GAVE US WRONG DIRECTIONS. When we tried to call them asking for clarification as they had given us wrong directions, the women on the phone began yelling at us, denying that they gave us wrong directions and continuously transferred our call. It took 10 minutes before another hotel representative came on to give us proper directions. We were lost in a city we HAD never been in for 10 mintues during the night. Then came the room. We specficially asked for a king size bed with no kitchenette. When we got to our room, we got 2 separate beds and a kitchentte. What made it worse was we asked for a non-smoking floor and throughout the whole week-end all we could smell was cigarette smoke. They NEVER once apologized for their mix-ups and behaviours. I cannot begin to explain how awful this hotel is. It may be cheaper than other hotels, but the abuse you experience is not worth it. In my entire life, I have never been treated in such a rude, disrespecting manner. I would not reccomend this place to even my worst ennemies.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: This was certainly not the greatest hotel I have ever stayed in. I picked it because it was three stars, had internet access, and was stumbling distance from the concert two of us were attending. I booked a single room with two beds for the four of us and it was acceptable. Well, with the exception of the bathroom. It was small and not very clean. The staff were rude and quite useless, they just seemed annoyed and unwilling to help no matter how polite we were. Which made it easy to stumble through the lobby drunk and singing at 1:00 a.m. There was a 'restaurant' that never did open the three days, two nights we stayed and no room service. None of the 'perks' of the hotel were available-pool, steam room, gym, and the TV was old and hardly worked. The room we payed for with internet access, didn't have internet access. They at least lent us an external wifi card but it still didn't work. And they never did give us any form of refund for that either. There were 'ladies of the night' out front of the hotel, but they were harmless and didn't hassle us at all. I had a great time, as did my other friend. But that was due to the amount of rum we consumed and an amazing concert. I don't feel our two friends enjoyed the stay as much as we did. I would not stay there again.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: Our church group recently stayed at the Primrose Hotel. We had chosen this hotel as it was downtown and they were able to give us a discounted group rate as we had 17 rooms in total. Everything went very smoothly. All the guests were checked- in in advance so no one had to line up at the front desk. The doorman assisted everyone with their luggage and picked it up when we left and brought it to the bus. The group in general was pleased with the rooms. We had a mixture of rooms with 1 bed and some with 2 beds. The service was great and we had a breakfast arranged in a private dining room which everyone enjoyed. I was pleased with the service I received from the staff both when arranging the tour and during the stay. We plan to make this an annual trip and will check back first with the Primrose before looking elsewhere for rooms.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: What is wrong with people? This is a good hotel we had no problems with our stay or room. The room was clean there were no stains anywhere, nice bed and dÃ©cor was good. People stay in hotels and expect them to be newly decorated for them rooms have to be used and accommodating. We use many hotels and in our stays, at Best Westerns all over the world have not had a bad one in the chain. Reception staff were polite and respected us, if you give staff respect we always find they give respect back, if you treat staff without respect what do you expect in return? Even housekeeping spoke to us in a morning and passed the time of day. The porterage was efficient and the bell boys were polite. We stayed with a tour on 9/10 September and would have no hesitation at staying or recommending this hotel again. My partner has worked in hotels for over 30 years and a lot of it in management and he would know a bad one as soon as he walked in. We normally take pictures of the rooms we stay in but unforunately did not on this occassion, if had they would have been put on here good or bad.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: Rude appearing staff. No smiles in any of the faces. Looks very disgruntled employees they have got. Could not sleep the very first night, A/C making too much of rattling noise. A/C not cooling enough. Almost decided to move to another hotel, but didn't because didn't want to go in hassle of moving the luggage with kids, etc. Reported the problem to staff, they say it is very common, not to worry. Not enough lighting. Gloomy room. No freshness feeling at all. Despite it being a kitchenette, it was a joke to have a little stove, no cutleries provided unless asked. Even provided ones were not washed by staff.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: Hotel staff were very friendly and accomadating. Vicky at the front desk was very nice and made us feel welcome. The hotel is situated in a good area and walking distance to Eaton Centre and many other attractions. We were there for a Chicago concert at Massey Hall and it was about a ten minute walk. We also experienced the subway and found it was very easy to get around. Over all our hotel was clean and we had a newly renovated room. I would stay here again!

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: My wife and I have been staying at the Primrose Hotel for years. Simply put Its a clean, well run hotel, with excellent service at the front desk and very large rooms that look great. We are working people with three kids and we dont have a lot of quality time to spend together so when we get the chance we come to the Primrose and here is why: 1) Our favorite room is reserved without us having to ask for it. 2) Our favorite bottle of wine is waiting for us in the room 3) Reservations are made at our favorite restauraunt 4) Staff know us by our first names 5) My wife gets a birthday email on her birthday 6) The staff truly feels like family TRY THIS hOTEL you wont be disapointed! !

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: My company recently booked a training session at the Primrose Hotel in Toronto. We were very pleased with the service and the meeting space. We occupied the Starlight room on the 23rd floor and found the room to be ideal for our training sessions. Because of the windows we were able to have natural light which helped keep people alert and didnâ€™t feel like we were stuck in a closed off room all day. We did order food and beverage and were pleased with the variety of choices available for lunches. The food was good and arrived on time and hot. The service was excellent and the session went without a hitch. Several of the attendees also stayed at the hotel and were able to get a discounted rate as part of the session. Overall our event went well and we do plan to hold our next meeting in the same room.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: Wound up staying at this hotel by mistake (my wife booked the wrong hotel online). Was a little worried given that it wasn't one of the higher end chains, but we were pleasantly surprised. Staff was extra friendly, room was large and clean, had a great view of the city and we were walking distance to just about everything. It's not a highend hotel, but it's great value for the price. Stan.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: My friends and I decided to stay at this hotel for two nights because the price was so good. The hotel was dirty. The shower was disgusting and there were marks all over the walls and carpet. The hallways were also very dim and can be scary at night. The elevators took forever! Be prepared to wait at least five minutes, and the doors sensors do not work, which was very annoying. The staff treatment was alright. They weren't that friendly. I had called down to front desk to ask for some extra towels and they were giving me a hard time. We had also asked the concierge for directions to certain areas in Toronto and he wasn't helpful. I guess this hotel would be ok for people who are looking to party. I wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for a nice weekend getaway or a family looking for a vacation. Spend the extra money and stay somewhere clean with friendly service.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: While I'd agree that the parking garage was hard to manoevre and the elevators were slow, that's as far as the negative experiences I had at this hotel went. From the time we got our parking permit until the time we checked out we had nothing but polite staff. The parking attendant was pleasant, the check in went smoothly,the room and the view was terrific. The sheets and the bathroom were impeccable and the stay was great. The restaurant buffet for breakfast was good, the wait staff was very pleasant. At check out the couple ahead of me had a bad experience with the management but the young fellow at the desk handled it with such grace that I wanted to applaud him. Everything on our bill was as it should be and the checkout went smoothly. It's not in the best part of Toronto but for the price and amenities it was a great value. My family has said that we should return at some other time.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: the hotel is centrally located and is very comfortable with a nice bed and rooms cleaned daily. The hotel however seems to be ageing with the air con unit making a loud grinding noise and shower water sometimes talking hours to drain from the bath tub due to a blockage. Overall, not perfect but good value for money. would stay again.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: I recently went to Toronto and reserved into the Primrose Best Western Hotel on Carlton St. I was given a discount as I was a senior so the price ended up being very reasonable. The hotel was in a good location and was close to restaurants and a wonderful greenhouse which I toured for an entire afternoon. The ladies at the reception desk were very pleasant and always smiling and very helpful in giving us directions. The room I was given had 1 bed and a small sitting area. It was very clean and comfortable and had very nice artwork on the walls. I did have breakfast in the morning in the restaurant beside the lobby area and was pleased with the level of service from the waiter and while he did make a small mistake on my order (he gave me potatoes when I asked for no potatoes), it was quickly rectified, and he continued to provide attentive service. My only complaint would have been that they have a lovely grand piano in the lobby and while I was trying to enjoy my breakfast there was a child playing around on it. I was impressed however that after voicing my concerns, the manager spoke with the parents and the child stopped playing. My stay was a pleasant one, and I would not hesitate to call them for a seniorâ€™s rate again when I next need a place to stay. We really liked this hotel!

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: This is a decent hotel, but factor in the low prices, great location and little perks like free wi-fi, and I'd say that it's one of the best I've stayed in. Not a luxury hotel by any means, but great value for the price. The room was big, clean and quite nice, the bed was very comfortable, there was plenty of hot water... the basics were covered. I found the staff to be helpful and courteous as well. A few very minor complaints - the bathroom was very small and a bit cold, since the only heat was from a small baseboard heater. The TV had something wrong with it and made a loud buzzing noise the whole time it was on, but since I wasn't there to watch TV that wasn't a big deal. I didn't eat at the restaurant, so can't comment on that. Overall, a good experience and I would definitely stay there again.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: We were tipped off that the lifts in this hotel are terrible before our arrival as we were on a tour. But we didnt realise they were as bad as they were, on the 3rd time of using them we got stuck!! Afterwards the Manager acknowledged that the lifts are in need of urgent replacement but due to the cost this has yet to be authorised. In the meantime people get stuck very often in seems. Indeed afterwards we saw on many occasions out of order signs on the doors at various times. We never used the lifts again after being moved to a lower floor. Atleast the manger moved us promptly but he's probably used to this request by now. Other than the hotel is OK, but far from great. The rooms are tired with many defects (both my rooms had faults including bulbs out, loose headboard and loose bathroom fittings. Breakfast was fairly average too. PS The hotel is right next to the redlight district too!

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: Went to Toronto for a conference which was being held at another hotel close by. Although it would have been more convenient for me to stay at the hotel the meeting was in, their prices were far too expensive for my budget. I got a room at the Best Western Primrose for a very reasonable rate. Even with the cost of the taxi to and from the conference, it was still much cheaper then the other room rate. The hotel was great, and I was pleased with the room. I thought the rooms were very well kept and the bedding looked new. I was also glad that the hotel had free internet access as I had to spend a great deal of time working, and not having to lug everything to a computer room instead of working from my bedroom was very convenient. The staff were friendly and helpful in arranging for taxiâ€™s for me, and always greeted me with a smile. When traveling on business again, I would not hesitate to use this hotel in the future.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: The Hotel is located fairly close to the centre of Toronto. We arrived to find the Hotel underging a refurbishment,which we were not advised of at the time of booking or through the Hotel website. We we awoken with the sound of drills and banging which was not good. We complained and was moved to a room a few floors below,that had already been refurbed. I do not understand why the hotel website did not advise of the works,and the management didnt seem to have an answer either. The Hotel was half full with students. Which although a little unusual did not cause us any problems.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed at the hotel the last week in August. We were very pleased with our choice. It's close to the subway and one day we walked to the CN tower - didn't realize it was that close. If you are in good shape, walking will get you to all the downtown attractions. The room was nice and very comfortable. I found the hotel staff very friendly and accomodating. One thing to mention - there are a number of prostitutes that work between the hotel and the subway station, so if you walk home at night you will run across them. But really that was not a big problem, they minded their own business.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for several nights in June, and were very disappointed. We had made our travel arrangements through Orbitz and didn't know how to cancel part-way through the stay, which is the only reason we didn't check out early. The first night there was no parking garage spot available, so we parked were the hotel recommended. Our car was broken into. The next day when we moved into the garage the attendant said we should never have parked in the previous location because everyone should know that your car would be a target there. The front desk staff were very unfriendly and always seemed to make matters overly complicated. They also didn't all have the same procedures. For instance one staff member refused to believe that another staff member had run our credit card through for a $300.00 account hold for incidentals until I showed him a copy of the receipt. He argued with me that they would only have gotten a $100.00 hold because that was their policy. They also tried to charge me with an extra night's garage parking and I had to get a manager involved to avoid the extra night's charge. I couldn't believe they were trying to stick me for a charge when I hadn't been able to park in the garage, the spot was supposed to be free, the spot was recommended by the hotel staff, AND my car was broken into while parked there. Also, the hotel is a high rise with only a few elevators which the staff also use. The elevators are VERY SLOW and we routinely spent several minutes waiting for them. The staff made no effort to give guests priority on them, either.

reviews.hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Primrose Hotel Toronto Downtown
reviews.text: The hotel is in a nice location, within walking distance of everything touristy. The price is very good and the rooms are large, the only issue with the hotel is its very dated and could do with a revamp. I stayed just under two weeks and I'd use them again.

hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
query: hotel room cleanliness and bathroom hygiene

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: I don't agree with the majority of the rave reviews for this hotel. It's best asset is the central Toronto location and beautiful public areas. However, the rooms are very average (no safe, mini-bar for example). During my stay, the first room I was given had a locked adjoining door. The room next to mine was obviously a large suite occupied by several people. Because of the adjoining door and no soundproofing between these rooms, I could hear their group conversations as if they were sitting next to me. Finally I called at midnight to insist on another room which they gave me. However, the next day after walking around in this room for an hour in clean white socks...I noticed that the bottom of these socks were filthy with dirt, grime. Obviously this hotel very rarely shampoos the carpets. My basic perception was that the rooms had a dated, unclean vibe. I will not stay there again.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: We chose this hotel for its location, which is excellent, as you can walk everywhere from there. It's also right next door to Eaton Center shopping area, where you can catch the subway and all the tour busses. We stayed in a one bedroom suite with a connecting dbl / dbl (5 of us). While the beds were comfy and we had plenty of room, the guest rooms are in need of a renovation. Had all standard amenities including coffee maker and fridge and robes . The rooms were clean, but when you looked closely, you would feel it needed a deep clean.. Ie around baseboards, walls and ceiling in bath, etc. service was excellent at front desk and concierge! Only had a drink in the bar, which was average hotel lobby bar. Didn't eat there. My biggest negative would be the super thin, over starched towels.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Room was clean but small- could say the same about the pool! Circuitous route to get to Eaton Centre inside- easier to go outside, although this was iffy at night, when lots of people gathering in dark corners between hotel and Eaton Centre. Staff very helpful.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: I stayed here for one night during a business trip. We arrived particularly late due to a flight delay so were checked in quickly which was appreciated. The rooms are spacious and beds very comfortable, unfortunately there was no bottled water in the room which was disappointing given the hotel standard but this is my only downside of the stay. There is however a coffee/tea making machine and the bathroom is ample sized. I wanted to order roomservice breakfast but had missed the midnight deadline for putting the order on my doorhandle however a quick call to reception and I was assured that this could still be managed. Breakfast arrived right on time and was delicious (scrambled egs, well done bacon, juice and tea...perfect!). Check out was again quick and our bags were stored by a lovely, friendly concierge. Upon returning to the hotel we were helped with our bags into a car that the hotel ordered for us and on our way. All in all a great (if very quick) stay in a hotel with a great location. Would recommend.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: We were attending a conference in the hotel so we basically had no choice when it came to picking a hotel in Toronto. Check-in : Everything went accordingly to plan. We were given our king size room which we had booked months earlier. Room : The room was just another hotel room , nothing flash but it was comfortable. The room consisted of a king size bed , small settee , coffee table and working desk with internet connection. The bathroom was on the small size with shower over the bath. Adequate toiletries were supplied. I actually like the aromatherapy orange ginger body lotion and managed to take a bottle home with me. Breakfast : A good selection with a chef cooking omelettes. Bar : We used the bar area frequently for pre dinner drinks and also returning home in the evenings. The staff were very efficient and friendly. Overall : The Marriott Hotel served a purpose and we had a comfortable stay. Our rate due to the conference was very reasonable so no complaints. The Eaton Shopping centre can be easily reached from the hotel. We also experienced a false fire alarm which was disconcerting as it took quite some time for us to get through to the receptionist to see whether we should proceed down the fire stairs or stay put..

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Quick check-in and check-out. Quiet, clean, modern room. This hotel has a slow parking garage elevator and forces you to call housekeeping if you want your bedding changed. Marriott also has uncompetitive internet access rates - because internet and phone are bundled together as a package. Other than that, a very good stay.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: I spent the better part of a week at this property. The room was comfortable and well-equipped...except for a small fridge that I was unable to obtain during my stay. The highlight for me was th staff. From the front desk to housekeeping to the restaurant/bar service, everyone was polite and very helpful. It turned out to be a very good choice for me.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: My boyfriend is partial to the Marriott chain, so when we booked to stay here we came with high expectations. We werenâ€™t disappointed. The king bed was super comfortable â€“ you literally just sink right in, it feels so delicious just lying down. I can see why they advertise and sell their own bedding. The room we had was a decent size and had a nice view. The location canâ€™t be beat, youâ€™re right in the heart of the city, right next to the Eaton Centre and steps away from the hive of Dundas Square. The valets recommended cheap indoor parking in the office building next door. We usually check out the amenities of every hotel we stay at but on this stay we had a long full day and just had time to settle in for a good nightâ€™s rest. We had no issue with noise, and we slept really well.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Stayed at the Marriott for three nights for a Conference. The room was very nice, a good view and the bed was very, very comfortable. The Staff were great and very helpful. The shower however was very touchy and the water was either scalding hot or very cold. Other than that it was great and I would love to stay there again.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: I cant believe that we stayed in the same hotel as the other people who have reviewed this place. It is probably the most depressing hotel I have ever stayed in. To start with the decor in the rooms is dreadful; mustard coloured walls, a mustard coloured 3D (dont ask) carpet, mustard cloured bed throws and an artexed ceiling only just over 7 feet over our heads. The effect in the small room was to feel as if the ceiling and walls were closing in on us. To compound this the air conditioning didnt work properly and we couldn't open the window. The bathroom was the highlight, fairly basic and clean but small with meagre towels and toiletries. Breakfast was reasonable but unremarkable and the service very hit and miss. The pool was pleasant enough for our daughter to play in but would be much to small for exercising in. The location is reasonable but quite a long way from the waterfront. During our recent trip we stayed in 5 hotels in Canada and this was by far the worst. I do recommend dinner at the 360 resturant in the CN tower, a wonderful experience especially as the sun set. If you have children under 8 they will love the fairground at centreville on the islands but avoid Wonderland unless you have teenage children who can go by themselves, the queues were over an hour long for many rides and it feels bleak and bland.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Stayed here for 7 nights. The hotel is in a great location and staff were efficient and polite. However, we were very dissapointed when we checked in to find that our sheets had stains on them and looked worn. The sheets looked as though they had not been changed when we checked in. We called reception at 3am to get them changed, they were apologetic and changed them immediately but even the 'new' sheets still had holes and looked worn! Dissapointed since this is suppose to be a 5 star establishment. Think it's in real need of refurbishment. Not good value.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Stayed at the Marriott for three nights for a conference. The room was typically Marriott - very nice, great view of the Church and gardens in between the Eaton Centre. The staff were wonderful! Bonus, no need to go out with a coat since the Marriott has indoor access to the Eaton Center...Shoppers Heaven for sure!!! Also had a problem with the shower - very hot...but not an issue. Had a Bloody Ceasar at the Hotel Bar...ouch..10$ for a small glass. Decided to go shopping instead...hihi! !

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: My husband and I are in our late 20's and stayed at Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre in early June. I have to admit that I am usually very worried about hotels and their cleanliness... but this hotel was extremely clean. The maid service was excellent and very prompt. We experienced no problems in this area -- like we usually do in other hotels. The hotel staff was very friendly and offered great service. This was our first time in Toronto, and they were very helpful in guiding us to certain places that we asked about... restaurants, shopping, bars, etc. This hotel has a great location and allowed us to walk to all places we wanted to go. The breakfast that is served at the hotel is wonderful!! It is a little expensive, but they offer a great variety. Unlike many other hotel breakfasts, this one actually has good food! One restaurant that you must visit - if you are interested in Italian food - is Terroni. The hotel staff may act like they don't know where it is... but it's on Queen St. For some reason, when we asked about it, they acted like they never heard of it - but it was packed, and they have awesome food!

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Stayed for three nights over (US) President's Day weekend-Friday to Monday. Check-in was smooth and the hotel had received my on-line request for a high floor and honored it. I chose not to pay for a concierge level room since the concierge lounge was closed most of the weekend. I got a discounted rate through the Marriott.com site and decided to take that rather than using points. The room was what most would call the "typical Marriott room." Excellent housekeeping and the usual amenities; plenty of room for one person. Bed comfortable; furniture, carpeting, drapes in good repair. Breakfast in the hotel each morning; buffet style with eggs cooked to order and nice selection of the usual breakfast items, breads, etc. The staff was absolutely wonderful both at the front desk and especially in the breakfast area. All very friendly and eager to please. Used the pool and whirlpool once; the area was clean and all the equipment in the adjacent fitness center in working order. The hotel is about one and a half blocks from the Dundas Subway stop which can be reached by indoor PATH walkway; hotel is adjacent to Eaton Centre and has an interior walkway to the Sears store next door. The front desk arranged for a private transfer to the airport on my last morning at 4:15 AM and that w ent without a hitch. Overall I was pleased with the stay and the location worked well for my planned activities.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: We had stayed in this hotel half-a-dozen times in the past and had been very impressed with it. The service has always been excellent. We often used to go on massive shopping trips and had to transport many large boxes to and from our rooms. The bell staff (usually women) would handle this for us cheerfully. I would often try to tip them, sometimes $20, but they always refused, stating that it was against hotel policy and that it was "part of the service". This happened all the time, and still did on this last trip. The location is also perfect for us: next to the Eaton Centre and walking distance to Chinatown and Queen Street. The rooms are large and the food in the dining room is decent enough. Now maybe our expectations of hotels have risen in recent years, or maybe we were just given a uniquely bad room for the first time, but our room was noisy! It was like there was no sound-proofing whatsoever. We could hear people walking and talking in the hallway and talking in the next room. This really annoys me, enough that I will not stay there again in spite of the excellent service.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: My friend and I stayed at this hotel in September 2011 during the TIFF weekend. The hotel lobby was very spacious, and well furnished with comfy seating for tired travellers to wait while checking-in. In addition to being spacious, the lobby was decorated in a modern fashion with booth-like check-in desk, complete with a very professional and courteous staff who checked us in promptly. The room was clean, spacious and even included a pull out couch! The bed was comfortable with lots of pillows. My only complaint would be that the room could be more sound proof. We definitely could hear some...*ahem* rhythmic knocking on the walls from next door. Aside from that, the room was great. As most people have already noted, the location is fantastic! For those looking for shopping, the Eaton Centre is literally next door. Everything needed is within walking distance, but public transportation is just as accessible. Great stay!

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Great service, friendly staff, good food - pity the room wiater couldn't go further than the threshold !!!! Oh and if you are a husband leave your wallet at home as the hotel is connected to the Eaton Centre; shopping mecca for wives !!!!! !

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: I have stayed here on two occasions with family and friends and really enjoyed both visits!! The rooms are clean and the beds are extremely comfortable...it was actually hard to get up in the morning! The hotel has a nice restaurant (not very cheap) and is attached to the Eaton Center by an indoor walkway. Made Christmas shopping an absolute treat!! All in all a great hotel - not a cheap stay but worth it in my opinion. Clean, comfortable, new...will definitely stay again if the price is right!! Front desk staff were not the friendliest...common to big cities perhaps?

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: This hotel was okay, nothing special. I think I must have missed what most people rave about. The room was a standard hotel room, nothing special or unique. The staff were welcoming, but not overly friendly. The rate was a little high, but the location is quite good. All in all, I'd say this hotel is ok. Price needs to go down a bit and staff friendliness up some.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Stayed for three nights as a family, couldn't be more central for all the downtown attractions, everything's within walking distance and the hotel is connected by a walkway to the Eaton Centre. The staff were brilliant with our little boy and the bar/bistro was lovely. The pool on the top floor was perfect for a wee splash around and the room was clean, tidy and a decent size.

hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
query: hotel staff service friendliness and responsiveness

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: I spent the better part of a week at this property. The room was comfortable and well-equipped...except for a small fridge that I was unable to obtain during my stay. The highlight for me was th staff. From the front desk to housekeeping to the restaurant/bar service, everyone was polite and very helpful. It turned out to be a very good choice for me.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Cannot complain about hotel. Staff was confused as to the concierge lounge, but that was it. Beware of tight turns in for parking garage under facility. You may have a difficult fit. Modern facility, quiet. Highly recommend. Best to call property directly for best rates. Marriott website or other sites may not have best rates.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Great service, friendly staff, good food - pity the room wiater couldn't go further than the threshold !!!! Oh and if you are a husband leave your wallet at home as the hotel is connected to the Eaton Centre; shopping mecca for wives !!!!! !

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Pleasant stay except for the night we made the mistake of having dinner in the main restaurant. We are NOT demanding restaurant a patrons, but both the food and the service was poor. Service was very slow, even though the restaurant was not full. When my husband's Cesar salad was served with chicken instead of salmon, he had to hunt down the waiter to point out the problem, and the waiter barely seemed to care. Food presentation was fancy, but the food didn't taste very good. I had some fried rice that was much too gingery; my side dish of broccoli was overcooked; the key lime pie tasted as if it came from a mix - you get the idea. And for this we paid fancy hotel restaurant prices - ugh! Rest of the hotel - room, location, front desk staff, etc. just terrific.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Quick check-in and check-out. Quiet, clean, modern room. This hotel has a slow parking garage elevator and forces you to call housekeeping if you want your bedding changed. Marriott also has uncompetitive internet access rates - because internet and phone are bundled together as a package. Other than that, a very good stay.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: The Marriott Eaton Centre provided service at its best. Everyone on staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel's downtown location is convenient for public transportation and adjacent to the Eaton Centre Mall. The mall can be accessed through the hotel without going outside. The hotel also has a nice indoor pool and hot tub for relaxing. My wife enjoyed the gym which had new and excellent machines. The rooms seem to have been recently updated and are well kept. Only downside was at 2am someone decided to light a cigarette in a stairwell and set off the smoke alarm causing all of the hotel guests to be evacuated. One guest's inconsiderate action should not reflect upon the property. I would highly recommend this hotel.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Hotel has comfortable atmosphere and lounge on main floor is relaxing. Check-in was a breeze. Room was perfect. Nice courtyard right outside hotel as you head to Eaton Centre. Checking out next morning was simple. Only hangup was the boarding pass console was not working for Porter. But hotel staff did their best to help.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: We have stayed at this Marriott many times but this was our first time back since the renovation and it did not disapoint. Rooms were spotless, and big enough. The staff was great right from check-in with a "welcome back" from every employee starting with the valet. Special thanks to Danny for being so nice with the kids he was awesome! One of the best features of this hotel is its proximity to the Eaton Centre as it is connected with a walkway so you can leave your coats in your room and shop all day. It is also right beside Nathan Phillips Square, which has a skating rink all winter. The buffett breakfast which was included with our rate was good every morning and better than most hotels. The pool is small but sufficent. We can't wait to come back!

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: We were attending a conference in the hotel so we basically had no choice when it came to picking a hotel in Toronto. Check-in : Everything went accordingly to plan. We were given our king size room which we had booked months earlier. Room : The room was just another hotel room , nothing flash but it was comfortable. The room consisted of a king size bed , small settee , coffee table and working desk with internet connection. The bathroom was on the small size with shower over the bath. Adequate toiletries were supplied. I actually like the aromatherapy orange ginger body lotion and managed to take a bottle home with me. Breakfast : A good selection with a chef cooking omelettes. Bar : We used the bar area frequently for pre dinner drinks and also returning home in the evenings. The staff were very efficient and friendly. Overall : The Marriott Hotel served a purpose and we had a comfortable stay. Our rate due to the conference was very reasonable so no complaints. The Eaton Shopping centre can be easily reached from the hotel. We also experienced a false fire alarm which was disconcerting as it took quite some time for us to get through to the receptionist to see whether we should proceed down the fire stairs or stay put..

Front desk staff were not the friendliest...common to big cities perhaps?

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: This hotel is very good. It's not excellent, but it is a very good Marriott. The check in staff were nice for the most part. The restaurant is not very good, so I would not eat in the restaurant unless you have to. The location is in downtown, so it's in the heart of things, but you have a fair number of homeless people and transients around. It's a little scary to walk around late night by yourself, but othewise, it's fine.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: This is the second time we've stayed at this hotel. We enjoyed our stay both times. The staff is nice and helpful. The fitness center is very nice and very clean. The best thing about this hotel is its location next to Eaton Centre. We had two days of cold rain but from Eaton Centre you can follow the PATH all over downtown and not go out side. We will definitely be going back.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: I do not often give hotels 5 stars, but In this cars, it was not the physical structure, that is so good, but he hotel staff that shines. The Hotel itself is fine and we had no complaints about anything. The staff took care of all ours needs and requests with enthusiasm and the concierge even went so far as recommend vineyards to visit for our side trip to Niagra wine country. They arranged rental car service for us as well as airport transport.. All very reasonably priced and on time. he only down side to the hotel is that the restaurant seems to be somewhat expensive. The food quality in the restaurant was very good.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: We chose this hotel for its location, which is excellent, as you can walk everywhere from there. It's also right next door to Eaton Center shopping area, where you can catch the subway and all the tour busses. We stayed in a one bedroom suite with a connecting dbl / dbl (5 of us). While the beds were comfy and we had plenty of room, the guest rooms are in need of a renovation. Had all standard amenities including coffee maker and fridge and robes . The rooms were clean, but when you looked closely, you would feel it needed a deep clean.. Ie around baseboards, walls and ceiling in bath, etc. service was excellent at front desk and concierge! Only had a drink in the bar, which was average hotel lobby bar. Didn't eat there. My biggest negative would be the super thin, over starched towels.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: This hotel was okay, nothing special. I think I must have missed what most people rave about. The room was a standard hotel room, nothing special or unique. The staff were welcoming, but not overly friendly. The rate was a little high, but the location is quite good. All in all, I'd say this hotel is ok. Price needs to go down a bit and staff friendliness up some.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Just came back from a four night stay at the Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre, and I was completely satisfied with this hotel. I was in town on business, and chose this hotel for its location. I had to book at the last minute and was able to get an excellent internet rate over the weekend days. The room was great: quiet, roomy, comfortable beds and good ventilation. Enjoyed the spacious bathroom with lots of counter space for all the toiletries that my daughter and I had. I felt that the hotel wisely focused on things we needed, like a coffee/tea maker, black out curtains, and a daily newspaper, while eliminating the nonessentials like mini-bar and robes. The expansive fitness centre is on the top floor and features city views, as well as a small pool and patio. My only quibble would be that the business centre charged $3 for 5 minutes of computer time, but if you brought your own laptop, you could use it for free in the lobby. I have to mention the housekeeping staff who were very efficient, and cleaned up our room almost as soon as we left it. All the hotel staff were friendly and courteous. The location was an excellent one for us because our event was just across the street, but we also walked to dinner on Queen Street, had many shopping choices (itâ€™s connected to the Eaton Centre, or you can meander along funky Queen West) and itâ€™s close to the subway. While we didnâ€™t get the free breakfast others have mentioned, we ended up at a tiny place across the street called The Daily Brew. A very friendly owner and you can get three eggs, two toasts, bacon and coffee for $3.99, so we became regulars for four days. All in all, a very successful business trip by day and very comfortable nights at the Marriott.

reviews.hotel_name: Toronto Marriott Downtown Eaton Centre Hotel
reviews.text: Stayed at the Marriott for three nights for a conference. The room was typically Marriott - very nice, great view of the Church and gardens in between the Eaton Centre. The staff were wonderful! Bonus, no need to go out with a coat since the Marriott has indoor access to the Eaton Center...Shoppers Heaven for sure!!! Also had a problem with the shower - very hot...but not an issue. Had a Bloody Ceasar at the Hotel Bar...ouch..10$ for a small glass. Decided to go shopping instead...hihi! !

query: hotel room cleanliness and bathroom hygiene

reviews.text: This is my second visit to Granville Island Hotel in eight years and both times have been exceptional; last time I didn’t know about tripadvisor though! I’ve been here for nine days and I couldn’t be happier. I looked at a few different rooms and they vary in size and view. They’re currently renovating all the bathrooms and the new look is beautiful; even nicer than the Hyatt Regency where I stayed a few days prior to this hotel. All the rooms have been remodeled with nice big screen TVs, very comfortable beds and nice décor. Even the bathrooms in the rooms where the bathrooms have not yet been remodeled are still very nice. I recommend room 326… vaulted ceiling with cedar beams, king bed, wet bar and a fantastic water view… at a standard room price. The service is fantastic… in nine days I’ve only encountered nice, friendly, helpful, courteous, attentive and caring employees. A special shout-out to Christine, AJ, Oleg Adam and Kim for their help. They go above and beyond and seem to really enjoy making sure the guests are happy. The housekeeping service is excellent; the room was spotless every day. At the hotel’s restaurant where I ate often, the service was attentive and friendly; they even went out of their way tonight to make a strawberry compote for the cheesecake because I didn’t want the cherry compote! They asked me if I wouldn’t mind waiting as they offered to make it from scratch… highly worth the wait. I also recommend the huevos rancheros for breakfast. The food is excellent and the view is amazing. Granville Island is an oasis inside a city. If you’re looking for an active nightlife then this isn’t the right fit. If you’re looking for a walk-able and relaxing spot then this couldn’t be better! I travel often, I stay in many nice hotels and I really can’t find any suggestions for improvement here. In Vancouver, I’ll only stay here from now on.

The room was so tiny we could hardly fit in it. No carpet on the floor, hardly any outlets and the bathroom was too small. We requested a larger room, since we were a group of three, previously booked and wanting an adequate room. We were told none were available. The room was small and dark and old. In no way was this a three star hotel. We left that night for a better place.

I made a list while staying there Good Points * Great location and really only hotel in the kitsilano area and only one on GI * Comfortable bed * Lots of drawer space in bathroom * Good selection in mini bar ie. Chips and salsa *The restaurant deck is very nice and modern and quite a gem....too bad about the service and the food. Bad Points * half renovated the common areas are nice, the bathrooms have no bath tubs but new bathrooms. The shower fixture although very smart looking are hard to use and are very sharp due to the sharp and clean lines of design. * Small rooms * We had a small balcony but had plastic furniture and latice on the floor (not nice) * The dresser, desk and minibar are still the old furniture (too many pieces and old and ugly) It did however have a flat screen tv which should not require a piece a furniture to hold it as it should be wall mounted. As I said the rooms are too small for all that furniture. * Lamp had burnt out light bulb...not a big deal but these things should be checked upon cleaning. *The art in the rooms are old and are of Delta, why not GI? You do have a art institute across the road. *The shampoo was in a ridiculous size bottle and if anyone figures out how to get it out of the bottle I would love to know. However the soap was a good and generous size. * The doors, wallpaper and carpets need to be redone. * The restaurant has a very limited and boring menu and the service is terrible. * Way over priced and not the price I had booked online Overall this is a good choice for the location and if it is within your budget, just don't expect too much.

Stayed here overnight 1 night for business travel. The place is a bit confusing to drive into at night if you're unfamiliar with the area, but my GPS showed the way. Check in was easy. The front desk clerk suggested paying $16 for parking permit "to be safe" in a 3 hour parking zone enforced between the hours of 9pm to 7am, even though I was outside those hours. I declined and had no problems. The hotel setting is very nice with water and dock views. The room was very nice, clean and new, a tad on the small side, but fine. High end bathroom fixtures, comfortable bed with premium linens, free wifi. My room was very quiet. Only room complaint was the old fashioned noisy A/C unit - noisy and musty smelling. I turned it off and opened the sliding glass door to get some cool air. Had breakfast at the restaurant. Service was fast, the food was very good and the dining room had nice water views. Overall, I really liked the place and would return.

I love the location of this hotel! Its perfect to be near the water and located in one of the greatest areas in Vancouver. I checked in no problem and they gave us a room they was sort of facing the water. Meaning you had to go out on to the balcony and look to your right to see water. The room also had a weird smell. I checked their website and discovered they allow pets, which explains the tile room in that room. I'm assuming the previous occupant was a negligent pet owner and allowed their pet to do their business everywhere in the room. We asked for another room right away and managed to get something that was equivalent to the one we had. I'm guessing that was fortunate since it was Easter and a conference was coming in a few days. The good stuff: the rooms are clean and tidy. The restaurant on the ground floor is excellent. The room service was great! Didn't try out the pool. Most of the staff was friendly. It was convienient to grab breakfast from the Granville Market and the restaurants in Granville are excellent. We went to the Pacific Culinary Institute and that was amazing!

This is a great hotel and obviously a favorite with discerning locals having events...they weren't really an obstruction to our having a great time, but did become something of a joke as both the hotel and adjoining park/marina/galleries are dripping with wedding parties. We had a great room at the end of the hall with a king size bed, and a connecting door to a smaller room with two doubles. The end room is great because even though it's small, 2 walls are window-sliders to balconies overlooking ritzy boats and water traffic. Restaurant was great. Bathrooms are super-luxorious. Beds are lush. We travelled with 4 kids and still had a terrific, romantic weekend!

I really loved this hotel. The location is cool in that you're in the only hotel on the Island, everyone knows where to find it, and it's central in the city. The hotel itself is reasonably priced, has very open meeting rooms with doors directly outside. The rooms are VERY clean (very), and the bathrooms are quite luxurious. The one drawback is that it's not that well insulated, sound-wise. I could hear the seagulls in the morning, and if there's a party in the hotel, you might want to bring earplugs if you're a light sleeper.

We booked the hotel on Hotels.ca for two days. The hotel is in a great location but needs some serious updating, sound proofing and desk staff needs an attitude check towards guests. The floors throughout are marble with an occasional scatter rug. Our room was adequate. Kind size bed, tv, marble floors small scatter rug on either side of the bed. We could hear chairs and people moving around in the adjoining room as if it was in our room mostly because of the echoing from the marble floors. The room was in a very quiet section of the property but the noise factor was a problem because of the large space in the threshold of the door and the rooms on either side. The elevator groaned when in use which was kind of scary.The pay per view movie was not working the first night, worked the second. We were charged $12 per day for parking and in-room water. The website's info said $8 per day for parking and complimentary in- room water. The desk staff would not look up on Hotels.ca the discrepancies we sited when checking out but they were very cheery and smiling the whole time while denying our information which was infuriating! In this day with gas prices so high and people not traveling as much, they seriously need a reality check or else this place will close down because of all the negative reviews.

I stayed at the hotel for a business seminar that was being held nearby. I couldn't stay at the seminar site as the hotel was booked solid from ongoing renovations. I couldn't have been happier with my "misfortune". The hotel was a short ride from the airport and the staff were very pleasant upon check-in and check-out. The in room breakfast was exceptional and reasonably priced as were the items in the mini-bar. Free wi-fi was accessed with ease and the bed was lavish. My one suggestion would be to get some in-room movies but I would definietly stay at GIH again.

We are a 40-something couple travelling with 3 small children. Since we'd heard that the rooms can vary in size and view, we requested (at booking) a larger room and a nice view, both of which were accommodated by the hotel. The highlight was the restaurant, which had the best food on the island and quite possibly in all of Vancouver's westside. Unbelievable. My husband tried a different beer each night that was micro-brewed at the hotel. He was very impressed and requested a tour of the brewery, which the brew-master provided for him. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. The walls were thick and the hotel had a quiet but friendly feel to it. Our girls loved the decent-sized hot tube with the windowed ceiling that allowed us to watch the starts at night. The location was ideal and the staff were superb. What would have made this hotel a 5-star for us would have been if the concierge had been more knowledgeable, particularly with transit options for exploring attractions.

We felt that we really made the right choice to stay at Granville Island Hotel. The location was perfect. My two kids loved walking through the island each day to get back to the hotel. We asked for a room with a view of the water and were very happy with the beautiful view. The staff was very helpful. We had a problem with the toilet running and somebody came up to fix it immediately. Everybody was very nice and I can't say enough about the great location. Would definitely return!

DATE: October 21, 2005; October 28-30, 2005 Initially stayed for one night at the Granville Island Hotel when we first arrived in Vancouver. Drove to Whistler and spent a week there. Returning to Vancouver we returned to the Granville Island Hotel for the remainder of our trip. We found this charming hotel to be more than we anticipated. The staff was consistently warm and friendly and above all very servicing. The rooms in the section away from the Front Desk by the banquet rooms seemed larger than those in the wing closer to the Front Desk. The bathrooms in the newer section had more counter space to place personal toiletries. That aside, the rooms were very clean and provided all the amenities needed to help make our stay quite comfortable. Hairdryers were provided along with lighted magnifying make-up mirrors (we found in the larger rooms). The mini bar was stocked sufficiently with a wide variety of refreshments and snacks. The Front Desk staff went out of their way to provide excellent directions along with helpful driving tips. The Dockside Restaurant has a beautiful view of the waterfront and the ambiance was warm and contemporary. The food and service were outstanding. What a great plus to have a class-act restaurant located within the hotel. Loved how this hotel is centrally located within Granville Island which made it convenient to walk to nearby art galleries, restaurants, shops and the famous Public Market. Driving to Yaletown, North Vancouver, Stanley Park and other surrounding attractions/destinations made it easy. The computer and printer located in the lobby for guests to use was very helpful. We used it mainly to obtain addresses and directions via Yahoo! or Google Map and simply printed the directions. Another plus was the complimentary high-speed internet access in all the rooms. Whenever we travel, my husband and I bring our laptop and check our emails daily. This also allowed us to research events and activities and various places to visit for the following day. We will DEFINITELY return to the Granville Island Hotel.

We stayed for 2 nights in one of the penthouse suites facing downtown Vancouver. The room was beautiful and very spacious with amazing views of False Creek. The hotel is not far from the Aqua Bus, taxis, and the Granville Island Public Market making it easy to get around. Our room was very quiet and well appointed. The bedroom area is so sound proof that we couldn't hear each other talk in separate rooms. There are wrap-around balconies off every room with chairs and a table. We had in-room massages provided by the spa just down the road and there was plenty of space for side-by-side table setup. We ate at the restaurant for breakfast once and had room service as well. Both were good. After living in Vancouver for several years, then coming back to visit, we found this hotel gave us an entirely different perspective of the city - one that we fully appreciated! Our only slightly negative comment was that the large kitchen area had plenty of wine glasses, but nothing else - no cutlery, no plates, etc. so that when we bought food to bring back to the room, we had nothing to eat it with. However, a quick call down to the front desk had all that delivered within minutes. We mentioned this upon check-out and they seemed happy to add those items to the room in future. I would definitely come back to this hotel and bring my kids next time!

We stayed there for a wedding last weekend and the location was handy. Unfortunately they just don't have the level of service that would make them a great hotel. The staff just seemed disinterested, especially at the bar and the front desk. And what kind of hotel charges for local calls?! Oh, and the sauna was broken.

This is a wonderful hotel with really nice staff and is a beautiful place to go for a drink or to stay. We arrived after a 9 hour flight from London on our honeymoon and thanks to our bestman the hotel knew about this and upgraded us.Then later in the evening the booking for the penthouse was cancelled, and guy at the desk asked if we would like to move. This was more than considerate and made for a wonderful first night. Apart from the special treatment that we recieved we found all the people who worked there to be really nice and interested in having a conversation. This is a very well set up hotel. The views of South Downtown are amazing (see pics).

We arrived from the UK tired and, hungry, and dirty, and found to our delight that we had been upgraded to a penthouse suite. The staff were very apologetic about the fire that had temporarily closed the restaurant, but when we saw our room, we forgot all about food. It was vast, with a dining room, 2 bathrooms - and a jacuzzi in the bedroom! We were so comfortable in the hotel that it was hard to leave it to join our cruise ship (where the bed was far less comfortable). The public market was amazing in the variety and quality of the food - nothing at all like the sad collection of vegetable stalls that you find at most UK town markets. The hotel staff were very helpful in getting us to and from the aquarium, giving change, arranging taxis. They really seemed to care about the guests. The hotel brought in free pastries and coffee every morning, while the restaurant was being refurbished. We ate them in the sunshine by the water, looking at the Vancouver skyline. It was pure bliss.

We stayed at the Granville Island Hotel because it was close to the Stanley Theatre and a $12 cab fare to downtown. The hotel staff were very good and accomodating, the hotel itself is good. The rooms are clean and comfortable, the bathrooms very nice (love the shower!). We had wished the room had a fridge that could be used rather than one stocked with liquor. Do people actually still use those liquor fridges?... The rooms are quite small, which was a little tight with two kids and my wife and me. The temperature control ( an old round dial type of thermostat) didnt work so we couldnt adjust the temperature, other then by opening a window. The hotel was reasonable value, and in a great location. We had breakfast each morning at Granville Island which is always pleasant (earlier in the day the better when its not busy.) All in all a good stay.

We chose this hotel for the last 4 nights of our 2-week holiday and were not disappointed. The staff welcomed us with great warmth and throughout our stay were genuinely pleased to offer help and advice on topics such as buses (including whether it was better to walk or take the ferry). Our room was on the ground floor, and I was initially worried it might be noisy as it had a view of the waiter's water station for the outside patio, but in fact it was very quiet, and we could glimpse the water through the shrubs which preserved our privacy, as well as people-watching. We had a room with 2 double beds for my husband and myself and our two boys (12 and 6), and the space was comfortable (though not generous) for the 4 of us, even when returning to the room for some "down time". Granville Island itself is fascinating - I could spend a fortune in the market, and the Kids Market is good for clothes and shoes as well as toys. The Dockside Restaurant in the hotel is superb, and we ended up eating there twice for dinner. Didn't try the breakfast we we tended to buy things from the market and eat them outside. If you're staying over a weekend I recommend booking for dinner as it was packed on Saturday night and Sunday lunchtime. A relaxed and comfortable place for families or couples.

Checked into the hotel on Granville Island for a 3 night stay and our first reaction was WOW! A beautiful large modern style room with lots of windows. Great kind bed with very nice soft linens and fluffy towels. Best shower ...the bathroom was huge with an amazing huge ceiling shower head. Staff were very pleasant and helpful. The restaurant too was really great and prices were in line with good restaurants in Vancouver. Although the hotel has parking for a daily fee, it is best not to bring your car as the island is definitely best seen on foot and driving on the island is difficult as pedestrians are everywhere.

We splurged when we stayed here and it was worth every penny. What can we say, with the great location, ambiance and first class staff , who met our every need. The Dockside Restaurant, with the large aquarium and with the in-house Dockside Brewing Company (the beer is good), offered a really enjoyable tasty meal. Our room was most comfortable and with its amenities, left nothing to be desired This is simply a first class hotel. Recommended

query: hotel staff service friendliness and responsiveness

reviews.text: We stayed there for a wedding last weekend and the location was handy. Unfortunately they just don't have the level of service that would make them a great hotel. The staff just seemed disinterested, especially at the bar and the front desk. And what kind of hotel charges for local calls?! Oh, and the sauna was broken.

We arrived and right away the staff were helpful. The one woman at the desk was dealing with an elderly WomAn that was taking a very long time talking. The woman at the desk saw I was waiting and made sure she got another person to come out and help me. I requested a room with a view and a rain shower and a king bed and I recieved all my requests, I was very pleased. The room was beautiful, the staff were very pleasant and the food from the restiarant Downstairs was delicious. They had very fast room service as well. Highly enjoyed our stay and the next time we have the money to go out for a nice weekend again, we will definitely be going back here :)

This is my second visit to Granville Island Hotel in eight years and both times have been exceptional; last time I didn’t know about tripadvisor though! I’ve been here for nine days and I couldn’t be happier. I looked at a few different rooms and they vary in size and view. They’re currently renovating all the bathrooms and the new look is beautiful; even nicer than the Hyatt Regency where I stayed a few days prior to this hotel. All the rooms have been remodeled with nice big screen TVs, very comfortable beds and nice décor. Even the bathrooms in the rooms where the bathrooms have not yet been remodeled are still very nice. I recommend room 326… vaulted ceiling with cedar beams, king bed, wet bar and a fantastic water view… at a standard room price. The service is fantastic… in nine days I’ve only encountered nice, friendly, helpful, courteous, attentive and caring employees. A special shout-out to Christine, AJ, Oleg Adam and Kim for their help. They go above and beyond and seem to really enjoy making sure the guests are happy. The housekeeping service is excellent; the room was spotless every day. At the hotel’s restaurant where I ate often, the service was attentive and friendly; they even went out of their way tonight to make a strawberry compote for the cheesecake because I didn’t want the cherry compote! They asked me if I wouldn’t mind waiting as they offered to make it from scratch… highly worth the wait. I also recommend the huevos rancheros for breakfast. The food is excellent and the view is amazing. Granville Island is an oasis inside a city. If you’re looking for an active nightlife then this isn’t the right fit. If you’re looking for a walk-able and relaxing spot then this couldn’t be better! I travel often, I stay in many nice hotels and I really can’t find any suggestions for improvement here. In Vancouver, I’ll only stay here from now on.

I really loved this hotel. The location is cool in that you're in the only hotel on the Island, everyone knows where to find it, and it's central in the city. The hotel itself is reasonably priced, has very open meeting rooms with doors directly outside. The rooms are VERY clean (very), and the bathrooms are quite luxurious. The one drawback is that it's not that well insulated, sound-wise. I could hear the seagulls in the morning, and if there's a party in the hotel, you might want to bring earplugs if you're a light sleeper.

Stayed here overnight 1 night for business travel. The place is a bit confusing to drive into at night if you're unfamiliar with the area, but my GPS showed the way. Check in was easy. The front desk clerk suggested paying $16 for parking permit "to be safe" in a 3 hour parking zone enforced between the hours of 9pm to 7am, even though I was outside those hours. I declined and had no problems. The hotel setting is very nice with water and dock views. The room was very nice, clean and new, a tad on the small side, but fine. High end bathroom fixtures, comfortable bed with premium linens, free wifi. My room was very quiet. Only room complaint was the old fashioned noisy A/C unit - noisy and musty smelling. I turned it off and opened the sliding glass door to get some cool air. Had breakfast at the restaurant. Service was fast, the food was very good and the dining room had nice water views. Overall, I really liked the place and would return.

I love the setting of this hotel. It is great to be on the "Island" and able to visit all the great shops and the Market. The two water taxis companies serving Granville Island make it very accessible to downtown as well. If you want to walk/cycle - it doesn't get better the the walking/cycling trails leading away from Granville Island. I had a room with a partial view and it was very nice. The staff were very friendly as well. I didn't have any meals at the hotel so can't comment on that. I didn't spend much time actually at the hotel so my interaction with staff was limited as well.

I travel a lot for business and I always look forward to staying at the Granville because I always get what I expect which is good value for the money and a very nice stay. The service from employees is always professional and courteous, the room is extremely clean, the restaurant food is good and the view is impeccable. The location of this hotel is second to none! Will keep coming back without a doubt!

We recently had an extremely bad stay at an American Sheraton hotel, and were a bit gunshy about staying in ANY hotel again...haha. But we were en route to Kelowna from Victoria and had some business to do in Vancouver which required a stay over. A local B&B actually recommended your hotel and we had a lovely one night stay with you. Staff were most obliging and friendly. Our evening snack on the patio was delicious, relaxing and we had a lovely server...again most helpful and obliging...and the view! Ach, beautiful!! We were initially worried as our room was adjacent to the patio and we feared lots of noise, but it was quiet after 10 pm, the beds were great and we both a great sleep, and really enjoyed visiting the market before we left for Kelowna. Now the traffic on the way to Kelowna was another thing altogether...we stayed too long and hit rush hour! But that's our fault! Thanks again!

It was a pleasure to work with the team at the Granville Island Hotel to set up 2 days of catered meetings. From reviewing the meeting room options to choosing menus and getting setup, the process was fast and smooth. The staff were responsive to requests for supplies and adjustments for our meetings. Feedback on the guest rooms from our out of town attendees was excellent. Pricing/value was impressive compared to other venues I looked at for these meetings.

This was our fifth Christmas getaway at the hotel. We're locals, but spend Christmas at the hotel each year, with our 3 (large) dogs and cat. The staff are friendly, helpful and always pleased to see us. The rooms are large, each with a small balcony and most have a view of the water. The food is excellent ( both room service and in the resto) and they have a micro brewery on site. With the hectic run up to Christmas ( I usually end up having to work right up to about 3 on the 24th), the arrival at the hotel is usually accompanied by a deep sigh... we're home!

This is a great hotel and obviously a favorite with discerning locals having events...they weren't really an obstruction to our having a great time, but did become something of a joke as both the hotel and adjoining park/marina/galleries are dripping with wedding parties. We had a great room at the end of the hall with a king size bed, and a connecting door to a smaller room with two doubles. The end room is great because even though it's small, 2 walls are window-sliders to balconies overlooking ritzy boats and water traffic. Restaurant was great. Bathrooms are super-luxorious. Beds are lush. We travelled with 4 kids and still had a terrific, romantic weekend!

Our stay was very satisfactory. The hotel is well situated. The service was good. The rooms are somewhat small and quite expensive considering the size. Food services are excellent. We stay at the hotel mainly because we like to shop at Granville Island. We appreciated the favourable room rate we got because of the course at Maiwa that my wife was taking. Overall, a very pleasant experience.
